sentences.zh: 宋將裴方明克仇池，立楊玄庶子保熾。

translations.literal: Song general Pei Fangming took Chouchi and set up Yang Xuan's younger son Baochi.
translations.idiomatic: The Song general Pei Fangming seized Chouchi and installed Yang Xuan's younger son Baochi.

sentences.zh: 於是假弼節，督隴右諸軍討仇池，平之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Bi was given the staff of authority and put in command of the Longyou armies to campaign against Chouchi and pacify it.
translations.idiomatic: Bi was then given the staff of authority, took command of the Longyou armies, attacked Chouchi, and pacified it.

sentences.zh: 未幾，諸氐復推楊文德為主，圍仇池。

translations.literal: Before long the various Di again set up Yang Wende as lord and besieged Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Di clans again made Yang Wende their leader and besieged Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 弼攻解其圍，文德走漢川。

translations.literal: Bi attacked and lifted the siege; Wende fled to Hanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Bi struck, raised the siege, and Wende fled to Hanchuan.

sentences.zh: 時東道將皮豹子聞仇池圍解，議欲還軍。

translations.literal: At that time the eastern-route general Pi Baozi, hearing Chouchi's siege was lifted, deliberated returning the army.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern-route general Pi Baozi, hearing the siege on Chouchi was raised, debated withdrawing his army.

sentences.zh: 弼使謂曰：「若其班師，寇眾復至，後舉為難。

translations.literal: Bi sent word saying: "If you withdraw the army, the bandit masses will come again; a later effort will be hard.
translations.idiomatic: Bi sent word: "If you withdraw now, the enemy will return and a later campaign will be harder.

sentences.zh: 不出秋冬，南寇必來，以逸待勞，百勝之策也。

translations.literal: Before autumn and winter are out, the southern bandits will surely come; to await the weary with the rested is the strategy of a hundred victories.
translations.idiomatic: Before autumn and winter are out the southern foe will surely come; to meet the weary with the rested is the strategy of a hundred victories.

sentences.zh: 」豹子乃止。

translations.literal: " Baozi then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Baozi held his ground.

sentences.zh: 太武聞之曰：「弼言長策也。

translations.literal: Taiwu heard of it and said: "Bi's words are a long-range plan.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiwu heard, he said, "Bi's words are the long view.

sentences.zh: 制有南秦，弼謀多矣。

translations.literal: In controlling Southern Qin, Bi's stratagems were many.
translations.idiomatic: In holding Southern Qin, Bi's stratagems were many."

sentences.zh: 」景穆總攝萬機，徵為東宮四輔，與宜都王穆壽並參政事。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Jing took overall charge of the myriad affairs; Bi was summoned as one of the Eastern Palace's four supports, joining Prince of Yidu Mu Shou and the rest in participating in government.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Jing took overall charge of affairs, Bi was summoned as one of the Eastern Palace's four supports, joining Prince of Yidu Mu Shou and others in government.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書令。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was made director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 弼雖事務殷湊，而讀書不輟。

translations.literal: Though Bi's duties were pressing, he never ceased reading.
translations.idiomatic: Though his duties pressed hard, Bi never stopped reading.

sentences.zh: 端謹慎密，口不言禁中事。

translations.literal: Correct, careful, and close-mouthed, he never spoke of inner-palace affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Correct, careful, and close-mouthed, he never spoke of inner-palace affairs.

sentences.zh: 功名等於張黎，而廉不及也。

translations.literal: His fame and merit equaled Zhang Li's, but his integrity did not.
translations.idiomatic: His fame and merit matched Zhang Li's, but not his integrity.

sentences.zh: 上谷人上書，言苑囿過度，人無田業，宜減大半，以賜貧者。

translations.literal: Men of Shanggu submitted a memorial saying the parks and preserves were excessive, the people had no fields to farm, and begging to reduce them by more than half to bestow on the poor.
translations.idiomatic: Men of Shanggu memorialized that the parks and preserves were excessive, the people had no land to farm, and begged to cut them by more than half for the poor.

sentences.zh: 弼入欲陳奏，遇帝與給事中劉樹棋，志不聽事。

translations.literal: Bi entered wishing to memorialize but met the emperor playing go with Attendant of the Masters of Writing Liu Shu, with no mind for affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Bi entered to memorialize but found the emperor playing go with Attendant Liu Shu, with no mind for business.

sentences.zh: 弼侍坐良久，不獲申聞。

translations.literal: Bi sat in attendance a long while and could not make his report heard.
translations.idiomatic: Bi sat in attendance a long while and could not get a hearing.

sentences.zh: 乃起，於帝前捽樹頭，掣下床，以手搏棋耳，以拳毆其背，曰：「朝廷不理，實爾之罪！

translations.literal: He then rose, before the emperor seized Shu's head, dragged him off the couch, struck his ears with his hand and beat his back with his fist, saying: "The court does not govern—it is truly your crime!
translations.idiomatic: He rose, seized Shu's head before the emperor, dragged him off the couch, boxed his ears and beat his back, crying, "The court does not govern—and the fault is yours!

sentences.zh: 」帝失容，放棋曰：「不聽奏事，過在朕，樹何罪？

translations.literal: The emperor lost composure, set down the go stones, and said: "Not to hear memorials is truly in my person—what crime has Shu?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor lost composure, set down the stones, and said, "Not hearing memorials is my fault—what crime has Shu?

sentences.zh: 置之！

translations.literal: Release him!
translations.idiomatic: Let him go!

sentences.zh: 」弼具狀以聞。

translations.literal: Bi set forth the full circumstances in a report.
translations.idiomatic: Bi laid the full case before him.

sentences.zh: 帝奇弼公直，皆可其奏，以與百姓。

translations.literal: The emperor marveled at Bi's public uprightness and approved all he memorialized, granting it to the common people.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marveled at Bi's blunt integrity, approved all he had urged, and granted the land to the people.

sentences.zh: 弼曰：「為臣逞志於君前者，非無罪也。

translations.literal: Bi said: "For a minister to vent his will before his lord is not without guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "For a minister to vent his will before his lord is not without guilt.

sentences.zh: 」乃詣公車，免冠徒跣，自劾請罪。

translations.literal: He then went to the Masters of Carts, removed cap and shoes, and impeached himself begging punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the masters of carts, removed cap and shoes, and impeached himself, begging punishment.

sentences.zh: 帝召之，謂曰：「卿其冠履。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him and said: "Put on cap and shoes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him and said, "Put on cap and shoes.

sentences.zh: 吾聞築社之役，蹇蹶而築之，端冕而事之，神與之福。

translations.literal: I have heard that in the work of building an altar, one limps yet builds it, yet attends it in full regalia, and the spirits bless it.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that in building an altar one may limp yet still build it, yet attend it in full regalia—and the spirits bless it.

sentences.zh: 然則卿有何罪？

translations.literal: Then what crime have you?
translations.idiomatic: What crime have you, then?

sentences.zh: 自今以後，苟利社稷，益國便人者，雖復顛沛造次，卿則為之，無所顧也。」

translations.literal: From now on, whatever profits the altars of state, benefits the realm and eases the people—even if you are overturned and rushed—you shall do it without regard."
translations.idiomatic: From now on, whatever profits the altars of state and eases the people—even in overturn and haste—you shall do it without looking back."

sentences.zh: 太武大閱，將校獵於河西，弼留守。

translations.literal: Taiwu held a great review and was about to hunt in Hexi with his officers; Bi remained on guard.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu held a great review and was about to hunt in Hexi with his officers; Bi remained on guard.

sentences.zh: 詔以肥馬給騎人，弼命給弱者。

translations.literal: An edict ordered fat horses given to the mounted men, but Bi ordered the weak ones given.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered fat horses for the mounted men, but Bi gave them the weak ones.

sentences.zh: 太武大怒曰：「尖頭奴敢裁量朕也！

translations.literal: Taiwu was greatly angered and said: "Pointed-head slave, you dare measure me!
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu flew into a rage and cried, "Pointed-head slave—you dare measure me!

sentences.zh: 朕還台，先斬此奴！

translations.literal: When I return to the capital I will first behead this slave!
translations.idiomatic: When I return to the capital I will behead this fellow first!

sentences.zh: 」弼頭尖，帝常名之曰：「筆頭」，時人呼為「筆公」。

translations.literal: Bi's head was pointed; the emperor often called him Brush Head, so people called him Pen Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Bi had a pointed head; the emperor nicknamed him Brush Head, and people called him Pen Lord.

sentences.zh: 屬官懼誅。

translations.literal: Bi's subordinate officials were terrified, fearing execution.
translations.idiomatic: Bi's staff were terrified they would all be executed.

sentences.zh: 弼告之曰：「吾謂事君使田獵不過盤遊，其罪小也。

translations.literal: Bi told them: "I think that in serving one's lord, making the hunt ill-suited to roaming sport is a small fault.
translations.idiomatic: Bi told them, "Serving the throne, giving the emperor poor horses for a hunt is a small fault.

sentences.zh: 不備不虞，使戎冠恣逸，其罪大也。

translations.literal: Not preparing against the unexpected and letting barbarian raiders run free is a great fault.
translations.idiomatic: Failing to guard against surprise and letting enemies raid at will is a grave fault.

sentences.zh: 今北狄孔熾，南虜未滅，狡焉之志，窺伺邊境，是吾憂也。

translations.literal: Now the northern Di are in full flame and the southern foes are not yet destroyed; their crafty intent watches our borders—that is my worry.
translations.idiomatic: The northern tribes blaze with strength and the south is not yet pacified; they watch our frontiers with hungry eyes—that is what troubles me.

sentences.zh: 故選肥馬備軍實，為不虞之遠慮。

translations.literal: Therefore I chose fat horses to stock the army and made distant provision against the unforeseen.
translations.idiomatic: So I kept the strong horses for the army and looked far ahead against the unexpected.

sentences.zh: 苟使國家有利，吾寧避死乎？

translations.literal: If it profits the state, why should I shun death!
translations.idiomatic: If the realm gains by it, why should I shrink from death?

sentences.zh: 明主可以理幹，此自吾罪。

translations.literal: An enlightened lord may be persuaded by reason; this fault is mine alone.
translations.idiomatic: An enlightened ruler can be reached by reason; the blame is mine alone.

sentences.zh: 」帝聞而歎曰：「有臣如此，國之寶也。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and sighed: "To have a minister like this is the state's treasure!"
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu heard and sighed, "A minister like this is a treasure to the realm!"

sentences.zh: 」賜衣一襲，馬二疋，鹿十頭。

translations.literal: He was granted one suit of clothes, two horses, and ten deer.
translations.idiomatic: He received a suit of clothes, two horses, and ten deer.

sentences.zh: 後車駕田於山北，獲麋鹿數千頭，詔尚書發車牛五十乘運之。

translations.literal: Later, when the imperial carriage hunted north of the mountains and took several thousand elk and deer, an edict ordered the Masters of Writing to send fifty cart-ox teams to transport them.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor hunted north of the mountains and killed thousands of elk; he ordered the secretariat to send fifty ox-carts to haul the game.

sentences.zh: 帝尋謂從者曰：「筆公必不與我，汝輩不如馬運之速。

translations.literal: The emperor soon told his attendants: "Pen Lord surely will not let me have them; you are not as quick as horses for hauling."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon told his escort, "Pen Lord will never let this pass—you are slower than horses for hauling game."

sentences.zh: 」遂還。

translations.literal: He thereupon returned.
translations.idiomatic: He turned back at once.

sentences.zh: 行百餘里而弼表至，曰：「今秋谷懸黃，麻菽布野，豬鹿竊食，鳥雁侵費，風波所耗，朝夕參倍。

translations.literal: After traveling more than a hundred li Bi's memorial arrived, saying: "Now the autumn grain hangs yellow, hemp and beans cover the wilds, pigs and deer steal the crop, birds and geese waste it, and wind and flood also consume it—the loss mounts day and night; I beg compassionate delay so it may be gathered in."
translations.idiomatic: A hundred li on, Bi's memorial arrived: "Autumn grain ripens in the fields, hemp and beans cover the countryside, boar and deer devour the crop, birds waste it, and wind and flood take more still—losses double by the day; grant a stay of mercy so the harvest can be brought in."

sentences.zh: 乞賜矜緩，使得收載。

translations.literal: The emperor told those at his side: "Pen Lord is indeed as I foresaw; he may be called a pillar of the state."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his attendants, "Pen Lord is just as I predicted—a true pillar of the realm."

sentences.zh: 」帝謂左右曰：「筆公果如朕卜，可謂社稷之臣。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yang Nan dang came in, an edict ordered Bi to send all his sons and younger brothers to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Nan dang first submitted, an edict ordered Bi to send all his sons and younger brothers to the capital.

sentences.zh: 」初，楊難當之來也，詔弼悉送其子弟于京師。

translations.literal: Yang Xuan's younger son Wende bribed Bi with thirty jin of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xuan's son Wende gave Bi thirty jin of gold.

sentences.zh: 楊玄少子文德，以黃金三十斤賂弼。

translations.literal: Bi took the gold, kept Wende, yet treated him without courtesy, and Wende fled to Song.
translations.idiomatic: Bi accepted it, detained Wende, treated him roughly, and Wende fled to the Song.

sentences.zh: 弼受金留文德，而遇之無禮，文德亡入宋。

translations.literal: Taiwu, because he was upright and had battle merit, did not add blame or punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu, weighing his uprightness and battle service, imposed no punishment.

sentences.zh: 太武以其正直，有戰功，弗加罪責。

translations.literal: When Taiwu died, the Prince of Wu was established and made Bi Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: After Taiwu's death the Prince of Wu took the throne and made Bi minister of works.

sentences.zh: 太武崩，吳王立，以弼為司徒。

translations.literal: When Wencheng ascended, he and Zhang Li both sat in council; their counsel did not accord with the imperial will and both were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wencheng came to the throne, he and Zhang Li sat in council together; their advice displeased the throne and both were removed.

sentences.zh: 文成即位，與張黎並坐議不合旨，俱免。

translations.literal: There were words of resentment and slander; their households reported witchcraft; both suffered execution.
translations.idiomatic: Resentful talk followed; their families were accused of witchcraft; both were executed.

sentences.zh: 有怨謗之言，其家人告巫蠱，俱伏法。

translations.literal: People of the time deemed it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries called it a miscarriage of justice.

sentences.zh: 時人冤之。

translations.literal: Zhang Li was a man of Pingyuan in Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Li was from Pingyuan in Yanmen commandery.

sentences.zh: 張黎，雁門平原人也。

translations.literal: Skilled in accounts, Daowu knew and favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in accounts, he won Daowu's notice and favor.

sentences.zh: 善書計，道武知待之。

translations.literal: Mingyuan valued his loyal uprightness, enfeoffed him Duke of Guangping, and put him in charge of crucial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyuan prized his loyal candor, made him duke of Guangping, and gave him charge of state secrets.

sentences.zh: 明元器其忠亮，賜爵廣平公，管綜機要。

translations.literal: Taiwu, because of his long service and merit, employed him as a chief counselor and made him Grand Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu, honoring his long service, used him as a chief counselor and grand minister of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 太武以其功舊，任以輔弼，除大司農卿。

translations.literal: In great military and state deliberations Li often took part.
translations.idiomatic: In the weightiest military and civil deliberations Li often took part.

sentences.zh: 軍國大議，黎常與焉。

translations.literal: For merit in campaigning against Helian Ding he was advanced to General Who Campaigns North.
translations.idiomatic: For campaigning against Helian Ding he was promoted to general who campaigns north.

sentences.zh: 以征赫連定功，進號征北大將軍。

translations.literal: With Prince of Le'an Fan and Duke of Jinan Cui Hui he garrisoned Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: With Prince of Le'an Fan and Duke of Jinan Cui Hui he held Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 與樂安王範、濟南公崔徽鎮長安。

translations.literal: Frugal, fair, and of great repute; on the day he left office his house had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He won high repute for frugality and fairness; when he left office his household had no surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 清約公平，甚著聲稱，代下之日，家無餘財。

translations.literal: When Taiwu campaigned in Liangzhou, the Rouran Wuti seized the moment to invade; Li with Minister of Works Changsun Daosheng repelled him.
translations.idiomatic: While Taiwu campaigned in Liangzhou, Rouran Wuti struck in his absence; Li and Minister of Works Changsun Daosheng beat him back.

sentences.zh: 太武征涼州，蠕蠕吳提乘虛入寇，黎與司空長孫道生拒擊走之。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Jing first took overall charge of affairs, Li with Cui Hao and others assisted in government, loyal in serving the throne and speaking only on public business.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Jing first directed government, Li with Cui Hao and others aided the rule, loyal to the throne and speaking only on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 景穆初總百揆，黎與崔浩等輔政，忠於奉上，非公事不言。

translations.literal: An edict granted Hao and Li each a thousand bolts of cloth and silk to reward old merit.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted Hao and Li each a thousand bolts of cloth and silk in reward for long service.

sentences.zh: 詔賜浩、黎布帛各千疋，以褒舊勳。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Wu Yu was established, Li was made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Wu Yu was enthroned, Li was made grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 吳王余立，以黎為太尉。

translations.literal: Later, when Wencheng ascended, he was executed together with Gu Bi.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Wencheng came to the throne, he was executed in the same case as Gu Bi.

sentences.zh: 後文成即位，與古弼俱誅。

translations.literal: Liu Jie, a man of Xindu in Chang Le.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jie was from Xindu in Chang Le commandery.

sentences.zh: 劉潔，長樂信都人也。

translations.literal: In Zhaocheng's time the Murong clan came to present a woman; his grandfather Sheng became household retainer of the princess and followed into Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhaocheng's reign the Murong sent a princess; his grandfather Sheng became a household retainer and followed her into Wei.

sentences.zh: 昭成時，慕容氏獻女，潔祖父生為公主家臣，乃隨入魏。

translations.literal: He was granted a wife and concubines; a son Ti was born, who reached Administrator of Leling and was enfeoffed Baron of Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: He was given a wife and concubines; a son Ti was born, who rose to administrator of Leling and was enfeoffed baron of Xindu.

sentences.zh: 賜以妻妾，生子堤，位樂陵太守，封信都男。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: Ti died.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: Jie inherited Ti's title.
translations.idiomatic: Jie inherited Ti's title.

sentences.zh: 潔襲堤爵。

translations.literal: He repeatedly followed campaigns with merit and was advanced to Duke of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned again and again with merit and was raised to Duke of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 數從征討，進爵會稽公。

translations.literal: Later he with Marquis of Yong'an Wei Qin and Meritorious General Yuan Qu attacked the rebellious Hu at Tujing and was seized by them and sent to Helian Qubing.
translations.idiomatic: Later he with Wei Qin, Marquis of Yong'an, and Meritorious General Yuan Qu struck the rebel Hu at Tujing; the enemy seized him and sent him to Helian Qubing.

sentences.zh: 後與永安侯魏勤及功勞將軍元屈等擊吐京叛胡，為其所執，送赫連屈丐。

translations.literal: Jie's voice and spirit did not waver; he called Qubing by his style name and spoke with him, his expression calm.
translations.idiomatic: Jie's voice never broke; he called Qubing by his style and spoke freely, his face unchanged.

sentences.zh: 潔聲氣不撓，呼其字而與之言，神色自若。

translations.literal: Qubing admired him and released him.
translations.idiomatic: Qubing admired his spirit and let him go.

sentences.zh: 屈丐壯而釋之。

translations.literal: Later he returned to the state and oversaw eastern affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later he returned and oversaw the eastern administration.

sentences.zh: 後得還國，典東部事。

translations.literal: When Mingyuan was ill, Taiwu supervised the state; Jie with Gu Bi and others were selected to attend the Eastern Palace and handle critical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingyuan fell ill and Taiwu oversaw the realm, Jie with Gu Bi and others were chosen to serve the Eastern Palace and handle secrets.

sentences.zh: 明元寢疾，太武監國，潔與古弼等選侍東宮，對綜機要。

translations.literal: When Taiwu took the throne, he marveled at his pillar-and-timber usefulness and entrusted great responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: At Taiwu's accession the court, seeing a pillar of state in him, gave him heavy trust.

sentences.zh: 太武即位，奇其有柱石用，委以大任。

translations.literal: When military and state affairs were discussed, court ministers all praised his ability.
translations.idiomatic: In council on war and state, every minister praised his capacity.

sentences.zh: 及議軍國，朝臣咸推其能。

translations.literal: He was thereupon promoted to Director of the Masters of Writing and changed to Duke of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to director of the masters of writing and made Duke of Julu.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書令，改為钜鹿公。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned west, Jie was vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: On the western campaign Jie led the van.

sentences.zh: 車駕西伐，潔為前鋒。

translations.literal: Juqu Mujian's younger brother Donglai resisted south of the city; Jie trusted the diviner's words that the day and hour were inauspicious, beat the drums and withdrew the formation, so Donglai was able to enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mujian's brother Donglai resisted south of the city; Jie trusted a diviner that the day and hour were ill-omened, beat the drums and drew the line back, and Donglai entered the city.

sentences.zh: 沮渠牧犍弟董來距戰于城南，潔信卜者之言，以日辰不協，擊鼓卻陣，故董來得入城。

translations.literal: Taiwu was slightly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu was somewhat displeased.

sentences.zh: 太武微嫌之。

translations.literal: Jie had long been in the privy council, relying on favor to act on his own authority; the emperor's heart grew somewhat displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Jie had long held the privy council and leaned on favor; the emperor's heart turned somewhat against him.

sentences.zh: 潔久在樞密，恃寵自專，帝心稍不平。

translations.literal: When there was discussion of campaigning against the Rouran, Jie said it was better to expand farming and stockpile grain.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated a Rouran campaign, Jie said they should widen the fields and heap up grain

sentences.zh: 時議伐蠕蠕，潔言不如廣農積穀。

translations.literal: To await their coming; the ministers all followed his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: and wait for the enemy to come; the ministers all sided with him.

sentences.zh: 以待其來，群臣皆從其議。

translations.literal: The emperor decided to go; he then followed Cui Hao's counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor resolved to march anyway and followed Cui Hao's advice.

sentences.zh: 帝決行，乃從崔浩議。

translations.literal: After setting out, he fixed a rendezvous with the generals at Luhun Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Once the army was out, he set a rendezvous with the generals at Luhun Valley.

sentences.zh: 既出，與諸將期會鹿渾穀。

translations.literal: Jie, resenting that his plan was not used and wishing to thwart the generals, forged an edict changing the date, so the generals did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Jie, bitter that his plan was ignored and wanting to thwart the generals, forged an edict and moved the rendezvous, so the generals never came.

sentences.zh: 而潔恨其計不用，欲沮諸將，乃矯詔更期，諸將不至。

translations.literal: At that time the barbarian masses were in great disorder; Crown Prince Jing wished to strike them, but Jie held that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarian hosts were then in turmoil; Crown Prince Jing wanted to strike, but Jie forbade it.

sentences.zh: 時虜眾大亂，景穆欲擊之，潔執不可。

translations.literal: They halted at Luhun Valley six days, yet the generals still did not gather; the bandits had already fled far off; they pursued to Shishui, did not overtake them, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They waited six days at Luhun Valley, and still the generals did not gather; the enemy had already fled far off; the army chased to Shishui, failed to catch them, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 停鹿渾穀六日，諸將猶不集，賊已遠遁，追至石水，不及而還。

translations.literal: The army halted in the desert; provisions were exhausted and many soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted in the desert; grain ran out and many soldiers died.

sentences.zh: 師次漠中，糧盡，士卒多死。

translations.literal: Jie secretly sent men to alarm the army and urged the emperor to abandon the army and return lightly; the emperor did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Jie secretly had men panic the troops and urged the emperor to abandon the army and ride back lightly; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 潔陰使人驚軍，勸帝棄軍輕還，帝不從。

translations.literal: Jie, because the campaign had no success, memorialized placing blame on Cui Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Because the campaign had failed, Jie memorialized to lay the blame on Cui Hao.

sentences.zh: 潔以軍行無功，奏歸罪於崔浩。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The generals were late, and when the bandits came they did not strike—the fault lies with the generals; how could it lie with Hao?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The generals were late, and when the enemy came they would not strike—the fault is the generals', not Hao's.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「諸將後期，及賊不擊，罪在諸將，豈在於浩？

translations.literal: " Again Jie's forged-edict affair came to light; the imperial carriage reached Wuyuan and Jie was arrested and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: " Jie's forged edict was exposed; at Wuyuan the emperor seized Jie and imprisoned him.

sentences.zh: 」又潔矯詔事遂發，輿駕至五原，收潔幽之。

translations.literal: Again Jie's forged-edict affair came to light; the imperial carriage reached Wuyuan and Jie was arrested and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Jie's forged edict was exposed; at Wuyuan the emperor seized Jie and imprisoned him.

sentences.zh: 太武之征也，潔私謂親人曰：「若軍出無功，車駕不返，即吾當立樂平王。

translations.literal: When the emperor set out on campaign, Jie had privately told his kin: "If the army goes out without success and the carriage does not return, I shall set up the Prince of Leyeping.
translations.idiomatic: Before the march Jie had told his kin in private, "If the campaign fails and the carriage does not return, I shall set up the Prince of Leyeping.

sentences.zh: 」潔又使右丞張嵩求圖讖，問：「劉氏應王，繼國家後，我審有名姓不？

translations.literal: Jie also had Right Assistant Director Zhang Song seek prognostic texts and ask: "The Liu house is fated to rule—to succeed the state thereafter; do I in truth have a name and surname?
translations.idiomatic: Jie also had Right Assistant Director Zhang Song seek prognostic books and ask, "The Liu house is fated to rule and succeed the state—do I truly have a name and surname among them?

sentences.zh: 」嵩對曰：「有姓而無名。

translations.literal: Song replied: "There is a surname but no name.
translations.idiomatic: Song answered, "There is a surname but no name.

sentences.zh: 」窮驗款引，搜嵩家，果得讖書。

translations.literal: Under exhaustive investigation confessions were drawn out; they searched Song's house and indeed found the prognostic book.
translations.idiomatic: Under exhaustive investigation confessions were drawn out; they searched Song's house and indeed found the prognostic book.

sentences.zh: 潔與南康公秋鄰及嵩等皆夷三族，死者百餘人。

translations.literal: Jie, the Duke of Nankang Di Lin, Song, and the rest were all exterminated to the third degree; more than a hundred died.
translations.idiomatic: Jie, Duke of Nankang Di Lin, Song, and the rest were all exterminated to the third degree; more than a hundred people died.

sentences.zh: 潔既居勢要，內外憚之，側目而視。

translations.literal: Once Jie held a position of power, within and without all feared him—men watched him sidelong.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jie held power, inside and outside the court all feared him—men watched him sidelong.

sentences.zh: 籍其家，財產钜萬。

translations.literal: When his household goods were inventoried, wealth exceeded tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: When his household was inventoried, his wealth ran to tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 太武追忿，言則切齒。

translations.literal: Taiwu, in retrospective anger, spoke of him with gnashing teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu, looking back in fury, spoke of him with gnashing teeth.

sentences.zh: 丘堆，代人也。

translations.literal: Qiu Dui, a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Dui came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 美容儀。

translations.literal: Fine in appearance.
translations.idiomatic: He was fine in appearance.

sentences.zh: 初以忠謹入侍。

translations.literal: At first he entered service through loyal care.
translations.idiomatic: At first he entered service through loyal care.

sentences.zh: 明元即位，拾遺左右，稍遷散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Mingyuan took the throne he attended at the ruler's side as remonstrator, and was gradually promoted to Regular Attendant at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingyuan took the throne he attended as remonstrator at the ruler's side and rose to regular attendant at the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 太武監國臨朝，堆與太尉穆觀等為右弼。

translations.literal: When Taiwu supervised the state at court, Dui with Grand Commandant Mu Guan and the rest were right assistants.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiwu oversaw affairs at court, Dui with Grand Commandant Mu Guan and others were right assistants.

sentences.zh: 及即位，賜爵臨淮公，位太僕。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, Dui was granted the title Duke of Linhuai and made Grand Master of the Stud.
translations.idiomatic: At his accession Dui was made Duke of Linhuai and grand master of the stud.

sentences.zh: 與宗正娥清略地關右，而宜城王奚斤表留堆，合軍與赫連昌相拒。

translations.literal: He with Director of the Imperial Clan E Qing surveyed land in Guanzhong; Prince of Yicheng Xi Jin memorialized to retain Dui, and they combined armies to resist Helian Chang.
translations.idiomatic: He with Director of the Imperial Clan E Qing surveyed land in Guanzhong; Prince of Yicheng Xi Jin asked to keep Dui, and they joined forces against Helian Chang.

sentences.zh: 斤進擊赫連定，留堆守輜重。

translations.literal: Jin advanced to attack Helian Ding; he left Dui to guard the baggage train.
translations.idiomatic: Jin advanced against Helian Ding and left Dui to guard the baggage train.

sentences.zh: 斤為定禽，堆聞而棄甲走長安。

translations.literal: Jin was seized by Ding; hearing of it, Dui cast off his armor and fled to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was taken by Ding; hearing of it, Dui threw off his armor and fled to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，遣西平公安頡斬堆。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and sent Duke of Xiping An Yi to behead Dui.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and sent Duke of Xiping An Yi to execute Dui.

sentences.zh: 娥清，代人也。

translations.literal: E Qing, a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: E Qing came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 少有將略，累著戰功，稍遷給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: From youth he had military talent; he repeatedly won battle merit and was gradually promoted to Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed military talent, won repeated battle honors, and rose to attendant of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 明元南巡，幸鄴，以清為中領軍將軍。

translations.literal: When Mingyuan toured the south and visited Ye, Qing was made General of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingyuan toured south to Ye, Qing was made general of the central army.

sentences.zh: 與宋兵將軍周幾等度河，略地至湖陸，以功賜爵須昌侯。

translations.literal: With Song general Zhou Ji and the rest he crossed the river, raided as far as Hulu, and for merit was granted the title Marquis of Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: With Song general Zhou Ji and others he crossed the river, raided to Hulu, and was made marquis of Xuchang for his merit.

sentences.zh: 與幾等遂鎮枋頭。

translations.literal: With Ji and the rest he then garrisoned Fangtou.
translations.idiomatic: He then garrisoned Fangtou with Ji and the others.

sentences.zh: 太武初，乃還京師，進為東平公。

translations.literal: At the start of Taiwu's reign he returned to the capital and was advanced to Duke of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Taiwu's reign he returned to the capital and was raised to duke of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 後從平統萬，遂與奚斤討赫連昌，至安定。

translations.literal: Later he followed in pacifying Tongwan and then with Xi Jin campaigned against Helian Chang, reaching Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined the pacification of Tongwan and with Xi Jin campaigned against Helian Chang as far as Anding.

sentences.zh: 及昌弟定西走，斤追之。

translations.literal: When Chang's younger brother Ding fled west, Jin pursued him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang's brother Ding fled west, Jin pursued.

sentences.zh: 清欲尋水往，斤不從，遂與斤俱為定禽。

translations.literal: Qing wished to go by water after him; Jin would not agree, and both were seized by Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Qing wished to follow along the water; Jin refused, and both were taken by Ding.

sentences.zh: 克平涼，乃得還。

translations.literal: When Pingliang was taken, he was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: When Pingliang fell he was able to return.

sentences.zh: 後與古弼等東討馮弘，以不急戰，弘奔高麗。

translations.literal: Later he with Gu Bi and others campaigned east against Feng Hong; because he did not press the fight, Hong fled to Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Later he campaigned east with Gu Bi against Feng Hong; because he would not press the attack, Hong fled to Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 檻車征，黜為門卒而卒於家。

translations.literal: He was summoned in a caged cart, demoted to gate guard, and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He was hauled back in a prison cart, demoted to gate guard, and died at home.

sentences.zh: 子延，賜爵南平公。

translations.literal: His son Yan was granted the title Duke of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan was granted the title duke of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 伊珝，代人也。

translations.literal: Yi Xu, a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Xu came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 少勇健，走及奔馬，善射，力曳牛卻行。

translations.literal: In youth he was brave and strong, could run with a galloping horse, was skilled at archery, and had strength to drag an ox walking backward.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was brave and swift as a galloping horse, skilled at the bow, and strong enough to drag an ox walking backward.

sentences.zh: 神抅初，擢為侍郎。

translations.literal: At the start of the Shengui era he was promoted to Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Shengui era he was promoted to gentleman.

sentences.zh: 轉三郎，賜爵汾陽子。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Inner Palace Guard of the Third Rank and granted the title Baron of Fenyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to inner palace guard of the third rank and made baron of Fenyang.

sentences.zh: 太武將討涼州，議者咸以無水草諫，唯司徒崔浩勸行。

translations.literal: When Taiwu was about to campaign against Liangzhou, the deliberators all remonstrated that there was no grass or water; only Minister of Works Cui Hao urged the march.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiwu was about to campaign against Liangzhou, every adviser said there was no grass or water; only Minister of Works Cui Hao urged the march.

sentences.zh: 群臣出後，珝曰：「涼州若無水草，何得為國？

translations.literal: After the ministers had left, Xu said: "If Liangzhou had no grass or water, how could it be a state?
translations.idiomatic: After the ministers withdrew, Xu said, "If Liangzhou lacked grass and water, how could it sustain a state?

sentences.zh: 宜從浩言。

translations.literal: We should follow Hao's counsel.
translations.idiomatic: We should follow Hao's advice.

sentences.zh: 」帝善之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 及克涼州，大會于姑臧。

translations.literal: When Liangzhou was taken, a great assembly was held at Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: When Liangzhou fell, a great assembly was held at Guzang.

sentences.zh: 帝謂群臣曰：「崔公智計有餘，吾亦不復奇之。

translations.literal: The emperor told the ministers: "Master Cui's stratagems are more than enough—I am no longer surprised by them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the ministers, "Master Cui's stratagems are more than enough—I am no longer surprised by them.

sentences.zh: 正奇珝弓馬士，所見能與崔同耳。

translations.literal: I am only surprised that Xu, a bow-and-horse man, sees as Hao does.
translations.idiomatic: I am only surprised that Xu, a bow-and-horse man, sees as Hao does.

sentences.zh: 」顧謂浩曰：「珝智力如此，終至公相。

translations.literal: He turned to Hao and said: "With intelligence such as this, Xu will in the end reach minister and duke rank.
translations.idiomatic: He turned to Hao and said, "With intelligence such as this, Xu will in the end reach minister and duke rank.

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「何必讀書，然後為學。

translations.literal: Hao said: "Why must one read books before one may be learned?
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "Why must one read books before one may be learned?

sentences.zh: 衛青、霍去病亦不讀書而致公輔。

translations.literal: Wei Qing and Huo Qubing also did not read books yet reached high office.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Qing and Huo Qubing also did not read books yet reached high office.

sentences.zh: 」帝欲以珝為尚書，封郡公。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to make Xu Director of the Masters of Writing and enfeoff him as Duke of a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to make Xu director of the masters of writing and enfeoff him as duke of a commandery.

sentences.zh: 珝以尚書務殷，公爵至重，辭之；

translations.literal: Xu said the director's duties were pressing and a commandery duke's rank too weighty, and declined;
translations.idiomatic: Xu said the director's duties were pressing and a commandery duke's rank too weighty, and declined;

sentences.zh: 中、秘二省，多諸文士，請參其次。

translations.literal: the Central and Secretariat bureaus had many literary men, and he asked to serve in the second rank.
translations.idiomatic: the central and secretariat bureaus had many literary men, and he asked to serve in the second rank.

sentences.zh: 帝賢之，遂拜秘書監，賜爵河南公。

translations.literal: The emperor admired him and thereupon made him Director of the Secretariat and granted the title Duke of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired him and made him director of the secretariat and duke of Henan.

sentences.zh: 拜司空。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed minister of works.

sentences.zh: 清約自守，為政舉大綱而已，不為苛碎。

translations.literal: Frugal and self-restrained, in government he set forth only the great outlines and was not harsh in petty matters.
translations.idiomatic: Frugal and self-restrained, in government he set forth only the great outlines and was not harsh in petty matters.

sentences.zh: 大安二年，領太子太保。

translations.literal: In the second year of Da'an he served as Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Da'an he served as grand tutor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 三年，與司徒陸麗等並平尚書事。

translations.literal: In the third year he with Minister of Works Lu Li and others jointly oversaw the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he with Minister of Works Lu Li and others jointly oversaw the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 薨。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子蘭襲爵，位庫部尚書。

translations.literal: His son Lan inherited the title and held office as Director of the Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lan inherited the title and held office as director of the treasury.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: Lan died.

sentences.zh: 子盆生，驍勇有膽氣，累有戰功，遂為名將。

translations.literal: His son Pensheng was valiant and bold, repeatedly won battle merit, and became a famed general.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pensheng was valiant and bold, won repeated battle honors, and became a famed general.

sentences.zh: 以勳賜爵平城子。

translations.literal: For merit he was granted the title Baron of Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was granted the title baron of Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 為西道都督，戰歿。

translations.literal: As commander of the western route he died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: As commander of the western route he died in battle.

sentences.zh: 贈雍州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Inspector of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made inspector of Yong province.

sentences.zh: 乙瑰，代人也。

translations.literal: Yi Gui, a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Gui came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 其先世統部落。

translations.literal: His forebears for generations led the tribe.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears for generations led the tribe.

sentences.zh: 太武時，瑰父匹知遣瑰入貢，帝留之。

translations.literal: In Taiwu's time Gui's father Pizhi sent Gui to present tribute; the emperor detained him.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiwu's time Gui's father Pizhi sent Gui to present tribute; the emperor detained him.

sentences.zh: 瑰善騎射，手格猛獸。

translations.literal: Gui was skilled at mounted archery and could grapple fierce beasts with his hands.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was skilled at mounted archery and could grapple fierce beasts with his hands.

sentences.zh: 尚太武女上谷公主，除駙馬都尉，賜爵西平公。

translations.literal: He married Taiwu's daughter Princess Shanggu, was made Commandant of the Horse Guards, and granted the title Duke of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: He married Taiwu's daughter Princess Shanggu, was made commandant of the horse guards, and granted the title duke of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 從駕南征，都督前鋒諸軍事，勇冠三軍。

translations.literal: He followed the southern campaign as commander-in-chief of the vanguard armies; his courage topped the three armies.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the southern campaign as commander-in-chief of the vanguard; his courage topped the three armies.

sentences.zh: 後進爵為王，又為西道都將。

translations.literal: Later he was advanced to prince and also made commander of the western route.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was advanced to prince and also made commander of the western route.

sentences.zh: 薨，年二十九，贈太尉公，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: He died at twenty-nine; posthumously he was made Duke of the Grand Commandant with the posthumous name Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He died at twenty-nine; posthumously he was made duke of the grand commandant with the posthumous name Gong.

sentences.zh: 子乾歸襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Qiangui inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qiangui inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 海子瑗，字雅珍，尚孝文女淮陽公主，除駙馬都尉，累遷西兗州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Yuan, styled Yazhen, married Wencheng's daughter Princess Huaiyang, was made Commandant of the Horse Guards, and rose to Inspector of Western Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuan, styled Yazhen, married Wencheng's daughter Princess Huaiyang, was made commandant of the horse guards, and rose to inspector of western Yan province.

sentences.zh: 天平元年，舉兵應樊子鵠，戰敗死。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianping he raised troops in support of Fan Zihe, was defeated in battle, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianping he raised troops in support of Fan Zihe, was defeated in battle, and died.

sentences.zh: 豆代田，代人也。

translations.literal: Dou Daitian, a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Daitian came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 明元時，以善騎射為內細射。

translations.literal: In Mingyuan's time, for skill at mounted archery he was made Inner Fine Archer.
translations.idiomatic: In Mingyuan's time, for skill at mounted archery he was made inner fine archer.

sentences.zh: 從攻武牢，詔代田登樓射賊，矢不虛發。

translations.literal: In campaigning against Wulao an edict ordered Daitian to mount the tower and shoot the rebels; not an arrow missed.
translations.idiomatic: In campaigning against Wulao an edict ordered Daitian to mount the tower and shoot the rebels; not an arrow missed.

sentences.zh: 以功遷內三郎。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted to Inner Palace Guard of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was promoted to inner palace guard of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 從討赫連昌，乘勝追賊，入其宮門。

translations.literal: In campaigning against Helian Chang he pursued the enemy in victory and entered their palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: In campaigning against Helian Chang he pursued the enemy in victory and entered their palace gate.

sentences.zh: 門閉，代田逾宮而出。

translations.literal: The gate was shut; Daitian climbed over the palace wall and came out.
translations.idiomatic: The gate was shut; Daitian climbed over the palace wall and came out.

sentences.zh: 太武壯之，拜勇武將軍。

translations.literal: Taiwu admired him and made him General of Martial Valor.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu admired him and made him general of martial valor.

sentences.zh: 後從討平涼，破赫連定，得奚斤等，以定妻賜之。

translations.literal: Later, in campaigning against Pingliang, he broke Helian Ding, recovered Xi Jin and the rest, and Ding's wife was granted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, in campaigning against Pingliang, he broke Helian Ding, recovered Xi Jin and the rest, and Ding's wife was granted to him.

sentences.zh: 詔斤膝行授酒于代田。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Jin to advance on his knees and present wine to Daitian.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Jin to advance on his knees and present wine to Daitian.

sentences.zh: 敕斤曰：「全爾身命者，代田功也。

translations.literal: The edict told Jin: "He who preserved your life was Daitian's merit.
translations.idiomatic: The edict told Jin, "He who preserved your life was Daitian's merit.

sentences.zh: 」以從討和龍戰功，封長廣公。

translations.literal: For merit in campaigning against Helong he was enfeoffed Duke of Changgang.
translations.idiomatic: For merit in campaigning against Helong he was enfeoffed duke of Changgang.

sentences.zh: 卒于統萬鎮大將。

translations.literal: He died as commander of Tongwan Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He died as commander of Tongwan garrison.

sentences.zh: 贈長廣王，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Prince of Changgang with the posthumous name Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made prince of Changgang with the posthumous name Gong.

sentences.zh: 子周求襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Zhouqiu inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhouqiu inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 車伊洛，焉耆胡也。

translations.literal: Che Yiluo, a man of Yanqi Hu stock.
translations.idiomatic: Che Yiluo was of Yanqi Hu stock.

sentences.zh: 世為東境部落帥，恆修職貢。

translations.literal: For generations his line had been chieftain of the eastern-border tribes and had constantly paid tribute.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his line had been chieftain of the eastern-border tribes and had constantly paid tribute.

sentences.zh: 延和中，授平西將軍，封前部王。

translations.literal: In the Yanhe era he was made General Who Pacifies the West and enfeoffed King of the Front Division.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yanhe era he was made general who pacifies the west and enfeoffed king of the front division.

sentences.zh: 伊洛規欲歸闕，為沮渠無諱斷路，伊洛連戰破之。

translations.literal: Yiluo planned to return to court; Juqu Wuji cut the road, and Yiluo fought him repeatedly and broke him.
translations.idiomatic: Yiluo planned to return to court; Juqu Wuji cut the road, and Yiluo fought him repeatedly and broke him.

sentences.zh: 無諱卒。

translations.literal: Wuji died.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji died.

sentences.zh: 伊洛前後遣使招喻其子乾壽等，及其戶五百餘家，送之京師。

translations.literal: Yiluo repeatedly sent envoys to win over Wuji's son Qianshou and the rest, and more than five hundred households were sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yiluo repeatedly sent envoys to win over Wuji's son Qianshou and the rest, and more than five hundred households were sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 又率部眾二千餘人伐高昌，討破焉耆東關七城。

translations.literal: He also led more than two thousand of his tribesmen to campaign against Gaochang and broke seven cities of Yanqi's eastern pass.
translations.idiomatic: He also led more than two thousand of his tribesmen against Gaochang and broke seven cities of Yanqi's eastern pass.

sentences.zh: 正平二年，伊洛朝京師，拜都官尚書，將軍、王如故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengping, Yiluo came to court at the capital and was made Director of the Ministry of Justice; his general's rank and kingship were unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengping, Yiluo came to court and was made director of the ministry of justice; his general's rank and kingship were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡康王，葬禮依盧魯元故事。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous name King Kang; burial followed the precedent of Lu Luyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumous name King Kang; burial followed the precedent of Lu Luyuan.

sentences.zh: 子歇襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Xie inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xie inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 車路頭，代人也。

translations.literal: Che Lutou, a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Che Lutou came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 少以忠厚選給東宮，為帳下帥。

translations.literal: In youth, for loyal honesty he was chosen to serve the Eastern Palace and was made commander of the tent guard.
translations.idiomatic: In youth, for loyal honesty he was chosen to serve the Eastern Palace and was made commander of the tent guard.

sentences.zh: 天賜末，明元出於外，路頭隨侍竭力。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tiansi era, when Mingyuan went abroad, Lutou followed and served with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tiansi era, when Mingyuan went abroad, Lutou followed and served with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 及即位，封宣城公、忠意將軍。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, [Lutou was] enfeoffed Duke of Xuancheng and General of Loyal Intent.
translations.idiomatic: On his accession Lutou was made Duke of Xuancheng and General of Loyal Intent.

sentences.zh: 帝性明察，群臣多以職事遇譴，至有杖罰，故路頭優遊不任事。

translations.literal: The emperor was sharp and perceptive; many ministers were censured over their duties, even to beating — so Lutou drifted at ease and undertook no office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was sharp-eyed; ministers were often punished for official faults, even beaten — so Lutou kept to an easy life and took on no duties.

sentences.zh: 性無害，每評獄處理，常獻寬恕之議，以此見重於朝，帝亦敬納之。

translations.literal: By nature harmless, whenever he reviewed cases and judged affairs he would offer arguments for leniency; by this he was esteemed at court, and the emperor also respectfully accepted him.
translations.idiomatic: Harmless by nature, in every trial he urged mercy — and was valued at court; the emperor heeded him.

sentences.zh: 卒，明元親臨哀慟，贈太保、宣城王，諡曰忠貞。

translations.literal: He died; Mingyuan came in person to mourn, deeply grieved, and posthumously granted Grand Guardian and Prince of Xuancheng, posthumous title Loyal and Upright.
translations.idiomatic: At his death Mingyuan mourned in person, posthumously made him Grand Guardian and Prince of Xuancheng, styled Loyal and Upright.

sentences.zh: 喪禮一依安城王叔孫俊故事。

translations.literal: Funeral rites wholly followed the precedent of Prince of Ancheng Uncle-Sun Jun.
translations.idiomatic: His funeral followed Prince of Ancheng Uncle-Sun Jun's precedent.

sentences.zh: 陪葬金陵。

translations.literal: He was buried with honor at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried with honor at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 子眷襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Juan inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Juan inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 盧魯元，昌黎徒河人也。

translations.literal: Lu Luyuan was a man of Tuhe in Changli.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Luyuan came from Tuhe in Changli.

sentences.zh: 曾祖副鳩，仕慕容氏，為尚書令、臨澤公。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Fuzhou served the Murong; he was Minister Director and Duke of Linze.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Fuzhou served Murong Yan as Minister Director and Duke of Linze.

sentences.zh: 祖、父並至大官。

translations.literal: Grandfather and father both reached Grand Provisioner.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather and father both rose to Grand Provisioner.

sentences.zh: 魯元寬和有雅度。

translations.literal: Luyuan was easy and harmonious, with elegant measure.
translations.idiomatic: Luyuan was easy in manner and measured in grace.

sentences.zh: 明元時，選為通直郎，以忠謹給侍東宮，太武親愛之。

translations.literal: In Mingyuan's time he was chosen Direct Attendant; for loyalty and care he attended the Eastern Palace; Taiwu loved him dearly.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingyuan he became Direct Attendant; loyal and careful in the Eastern Palace, Taiwu cherished him.

sentences.zh: 即位，以為中書侍郎，寵待彌渥。

translations.literal: When [Taiwu] took the throne, he was made Secretariat Gentleman; favor and treatment grew ever richer.
translations.idiomatic: On accession he was made Secretariat Gentleman; favor deepened.

sentences.zh: 而魯元益加謹肅，帝愈親待之。

translations.literal: Yet Luyuan became all the more grave and respectful; the emperor drew still closer to him.
translations.idiomatic: Luyuan grew only more grave; the emperor drew closer still.

sentences.zh: 內外大臣，莫不敬憚。

translations.literal: Within and without, great ministers — none did not respect and fear him.
translations.idiomatic: Inside and outside the court, every great minister feared him.

sentences.zh: 性多容納，善與人交，好掩人過揚人美，由是公卿咸親附之。

translations.literal: By nature he bore much and was skilled at friendship; he liked to cover others' faults and proclaim their merits — thus nobles and ministers all drew near to him.
translations.idiomatic: He bore much, befriended well, covered faults and praised merit — nobles and ministers all clung to him.

sentences.zh: 以工書有文才，累遷中書監，領秘書事。

translations.literal: For skill in calligraphy and literary talent he was repeatedly promoted to Supervisor of the Secretariat, overseeing the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in calligraphy and letters, he rose to Secretariat Supervisor and oversaw the archives.

sentences.zh: 賜爵襄城公，贈其父為信都侯。

translations.literal: He was granted the title Duke of Xiangcheng and his father was enfeoffed Marquis of Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Duke of Xiangcheng; his father was enfeoffed Marquis of Xindu.

sentences.zh: 從征赫連昌，太武親追擊，入其城門，魯元隨帝出入。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Helian Chang, Taiwu personally pursued; entering the city gate, Luyuan followed the emperor in and out.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against Helian Chang, Taiwu charged in person; Luyuan went in and out at his side.

sentences.zh: 是日微魯元，幾至危殆。

translations.literal: That day, had Luyuan been absent, [the emperor] would nearly have reached peril.
translations.idiomatic: That day without Luyuan he would nearly have been lost.

sentences.zh: 後遷太保、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Grand Guardian and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became Grand Guardian and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 帝貴異之，臨幸其第，不出旬日。

translations.literal: The emperor prized him exceptionally; within ten days he visited his residence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor prized him; within ten days he visited his house.

sentences.zh: 欲其居近，易往來，乃賜甲第于宮門南。

translations.literal: Wishing him to live near and easy to visit, he granted a fine mansion south of the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: Wanting him near at hand, he gave a fine mansion south of the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 衣食車馬皆乘輿之副。

translations.literal: Food, clothing, carriages, and horses were all duplicates of the imperial equipage.
translations.idiomatic: Food, dress, carriages, and horses matched the imperial train.

sentences.zh: 真君三年，駕幸陰山，魯元以疾不從。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenjun, the emperor toured Yinshan; Luyuan did not follow because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenjun year three the emperor went to Yinshan; Luyuan stayed behind, ill.

sentences.zh: 侍臣問疾，醫藥傳驛，相屬於路。

translations.literal: Attending ministers inquired after his illness; medicine traveled by relay post, one after another on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers asked after him; medicine came by relay, one courier after another.

sentences.zh: 及薨，帝甚悼惜之，還臨其喪，哭之哀慟。

translations.literal: When he died the emperor grieved deeply; returning, he came to the mourning hall and wept with piercing sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: At his death the emperor grieved; on return he came to the bier and wept bitterly.

sentences.zh: 東西二宮，命大官日送奠。

translations.literal: East and West Palaces ordered the Grand Provisioner to send offerings daily.
translations.idiomatic: Both palaces ordered daily offerings from the Grand Provisioner.

sentences.zh: 晨昏哭臨，訖則備奏鐘鼓伎樂。

translations.literal: Morning and evening the emperor came to weep; when finished he had bells, drums, performers, and music prepared and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Morning and evening he came to mourn; when he left, bells, drums, and music were made ready.

sentences.zh: 輿駕比葬三臨之。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage came three times for the burial.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage came thrice to the burial.

sentences.zh: 喪禮依安城王叔孫俊故事而賵送有加。

translations.literal: Funeral rites followed Prince of Ancheng Uncle-Sun Jun's precedent, yet condolence gifts were increased.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral rites followed Uncle-Sun Jun's precedent, with added gifts of condolence.

sentences.zh: 贈襄城王，諡曰孝。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Xiangcheng, posthumous title Filial.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously made Prince of Xiangcheng, styled Filial.

sentences.zh: 葬於崞山，為建碑闕。

translations.literal: Buried at Guo Mountain; a stele and gate-towers were built.
translations.idiomatic: Buried at Guo Mountain with stele and gate-towers raised.

sentences.zh: 自魏興，貴臣恩寵，無與為比。

translations.literal: Since Wei rose, no favored minister's grace and favor had been his equal.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Wei rose, no minister had known such favor.

sentences.zh: 魯元少子內，給侍東宮。

translations.literal: Luyuan's younger son Nei attended the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His younger son Nei served the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 景穆深昵之，常與臥起，同衣食。

translations.literal: Jingmu was deeply intimate with him, often sharing bed and rising, food and clothing alike.
translations.idiomatic: Jingmu doted on him — they slept and woke together, shared food and dress.

sentences.zh: 父子有寵兩宮，勢傾天下。

translations.literal: Father and son held favor in both palaces; their power bent the world.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son held both palaces; their power bent the realm.

sentences.zh: 內性寬厚，有父風，而恭慎不及。

translations.literal: Nei was generous by nature, with his father's manner, yet did not match his father's respect and caution.
translations.idiomatic: Nei was open-hearted like his father, but less careful.

sentences.zh: 正平初，宮臣伏誅。

translations.literal: At the start of Zhengping, palace officers were executed.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Zhengping, palace officers were put to death.

sentences.zh: 太武以魯元故，唯殺內而厚撫其兄弟。

translations.literal: For Luyuan's sake Taiwu killed only Nei and treated his brothers with generous favor.
translations.idiomatic: For Luyuan's sake Taiwu killed only Nei and treated his brothers generously.

sentences.zh: 來大幹，代人也。

translations.literal: Lai Dagan was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Dagan was a man of Dai.

sentences.zh: 父初真，從道武避難叱候山，參創業功。

translations.literal: His father Chuzhen, fleeing hardship with Emperor Daowu at Chihou Mountain, shared in founding merit.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chuzhen fled with Daowu to Chihou Mountain and shared in founding the state.

sentences.zh: 官至後將軍，武原侯，與在八議。

translations.literal: He reached Rear General, Marquis of Wuyuan, and stood among the Eight Clans of Punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Rear General and Marquis of Wuyuan, among the Eight Clans of Punishment.

sentences.zh: 大幹驍果善騎射。

translations.literal: Dagan was fierce and skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Dagan was fierce and masterful on horseback with bow.

sentences.zh: 永興初，襲爵，位中散。

translations.literal: At the start of Yongxing he inherited the title and held Central Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongxing's start he inherited the title as Central Attendant.

sentences.zh: 至於朝賀之日，大幹常著禦鎧，盤馬殿庭，朝臣莫不嗟歎。

translations.literal: On days of court congratulation Dagan would wear imperial armor and wheel his horse in the palace courtyard; court ministers all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: On congratulation days he wore imperial armor and wheeled his horse in the hall; ministers sighed in wonder.

sentences.zh: 遷內三郎、幢將，典宿衛禁旅。

translations.literal: He was transferred Inner Third Baron, Pennon General, overseeing the night guard and forbidden troops.
translations.idiomatic: He became Inner Third Baron and Pennon General, commanding the night guard.

sentences.zh: 大幹用法嚴明，上下齊肅。

translations.literal: Dagan applied the law with stern clarity; above and below were uniformly disciplined.
translations.idiomatic: He enforced the law sternly; all ranks stood in order.

sentences.zh: 嘗從明元校獵，見獸在高岩上，持槊直前刺之，應手而死，帝嘉其勇壯。

translations.literal: Once following Mingyuan on a hunting drill, he saw a beast on a high cliff; spear in hand he went straight forward and stabbed it — it died at the stroke; the emperor praised his brave strength.
translations.idiomatic: Hunting with Mingyuan he saw game on a high cliff, ran his spear straight in, and killed it at a stroke; the emperor praised his courage.

sentences.zh: 太武踐阼，與襄城公盧魯元等七人俱為常侍，常持仗侍衛，晝夜不離左右。

translations.literal: When Taiwu took the throne, with Duke of Xiangcheng Lu Luyuan and six others he was all made Regular Attendant, constantly holding arms to attend and guard, day and night never leaving the side.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiwu acceded, he and Lu Luyuan and six others became Regular Attendants, armed at the emperor's side day and night.

sentences.zh: 累從征伐，以戰功賜爵廬陵公，鎮雲中，兼統白道軍事。

translations.literal: Repeatedly following campaigns, for battle merit he was granted Duke of Luling, garrisoned Yunzhong, and concurrently commanded White Road military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On repeated campaigns he was made Duke of Luling, garrisoned Yunzhong, and commanded the White Road.

sentences.zh: 太武以其壯勇，數有戰功，兼悉北境險要，詔使巡撫六鎮，以防寇虜。

translations.literal: Taiwu, because of his stalwart courage, repeated battle merit, and thorough knowledge of the northern border's passes and strongpoints, ordered him to tour and pacify the six garrisons to guard against raiders.
translations.idiomatic: For courage, merit, and knowledge of the northern passes Taiwu sent him to tour the six garrisons against raiders.

sentences.zh: 經略佈置，甚得事宜。

translations.literal: His planning and disposition were very fit to circumstance.
translations.idiomatic: His dispositions suited the terrain well.

sentences.zh: 後吐京胡反，以大幹為都將，討平之。

translations.literal: Later the Tujing Hu rebelled; Dagan was made chief commander and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tujing Hu rebelled, Dagan was chief commander and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 在吐京卒。

translations.literal: He died at Tujing.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Tujing.

sentences.zh: 喪還，停于平城南。

translations.literal: The coffin returned and halted south of Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The coffin returned and halted south of Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 太武出遊還，見而問之，左右以對，帝悼歎者良久。

translations.literal: Taiwu returned from an outing, saw it, and asked; attendants answered; the emperor mourned and sighed for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu came back from an outing, saw it, asked, and sighed long in grief.

sentences.zh: 詔聽其喪入殯城內。

translations.literal: An edict permitted the coffin to enter the city for encoffining.
translations.idiomatic: An edict let the coffin enter the city for encoffining.

sentences.zh: 贈司空，諡莊公。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Minister of Works, posthumous title Duke Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously Minister of Works, styled Duke Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子丘頹襲爵，降為晉興侯。

translations.literal: His son Qiutui inherited the title, reduced to Marquis of Jinxing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qiutui inherited, reduced to Marquis of Jinxing.

sentences.zh: 宿石，朔方人，赫連屈丐弟文陳之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Su Shi was a man of Shuofang, great-grandson of Wenchen, younger brother of Helian Qubukan.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi was from Shuofang, great-grandson of Wenchen, Helian Qubukan's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 天興中，文陳父子歸魏，道武嘉之，以宗女妻焉，拜上將軍。

translations.literal: In Tianxing, Wenchen father and son submitted to Wei; Daowu commended them and gave an imperial clanswoman in marriage, appointing Senior General.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianxing, Wenchen and his son came to Wei; Daowu praised them, married them an imperial clanswoman, and made Senior General.

sentences.zh: 祖若豆根，明元時賜姓宿氏，襲上將軍。

translations.literal: Grandfather Ruodougen, in Mingyuan's time was granted the surname Su, inheriting Senior General.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Ruodougen took the surname Su under Mingyuan and inherited Senior General.

sentences.zh: 父遝幹，從太武征平涼有功，賜爵漢安男。

translations.literal: Father Diggan followed Taiwu in the Pingliang campaign with merit and was granted Baron of Han'an.
translations.idiomatic: Father Diggan followed Taiwu to Pingliang with merit and was made Baron of Han'an.

sentences.zh: 後從討蠕蠕，戰沒。

translations.literal: Later following the campaign against the Rouran he died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Later campaigning against the Rouran he fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 石年十三襲爵，擢為中散，遷內行令。

translations.literal: Shi at thirteen inherited the title, was promoted Central Attendant, and transferred Inner Conduct Director.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen Shi inherited, rose to Central Attendant, then Inner Conduct Director.

sentences.zh: 從于苑中游獵，石走馬引前，道峻馬倒，殞絕，久之乃蘇。

translations.literal: Following the emperor hunting in the park, Shi ran his horse ahead; the road was steep and the horse fell — he was dead a long while before reviving.
translations.idiomatic: Hunting in the park Shi rode ahead; the path was steep, his horse fell, and he lay as dead long before waking.

sentences.zh: 由是御馬得制。

translations.literal: From this the imperial horse was brought under control.
translations.idiomatic: From this the imperial horse was mastered.

sentences.zh: 文成嘉之，賜以綿帛、駿馬，改爵義陽子。

translations.literal: Wencheng commended him, granted silk and fine horses, and changed his title to Viscount of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng praised him, gave silk and fine horses, and made him Viscount of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 又常從獵，文成親欲射猛獸。

translations.literal: Again on a hunt Wencheng himself wished to shoot fierce beasts.
translations.idiomatic: Again on a hunt Wencheng meant to shoot fierce beasts himself.

sentences.zh: 石叩馬諫，引帝至高原上。

translations.literal: Shi knocked his horse and remonstrated, leading the emperor to a high plateau.
translations.idiomatic: Shi checked his horse and urged him to a high plateau.

sentences.zh: 後猛獸騰躍殺人。

translations.literal: Later the fierce beast leapt and killed a man.
translations.idiomatic: Later the beast sprang and killed a man.

sentences.zh: 褒美其忠，許後有犯罪，宥而勿坐，賜駿馬一疋。

translations.literal: Praising his loyalty, [the emperor] granted that if hereafter he committed crime he should be pardoned and not punished, and gave one fine horse.
translations.idiomatic: For his loyalty he was promised future crimes pardoned, and given a fine horse.

sentences.zh: 尚上谷公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: He married Princess of Shanggu and was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards Consort.
translations.idiomatic: He married the Princess of Shanggu and became Commandant of the Horse Guards Consort.

sentences.zh: 位吏部尚書，進爵太山公，為北征中道都大將。

translations.literal: He held Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, advanced to Duke of Mount Tai, and was Grand General of the Middle Route of the Northern Expedition.
translations.idiomatic: He was Minister of Personnel, Duke of Mount Tai, and Grand General of the Northern Expedition's middle route.

sentences.zh: 卒，追贈太原王，諡康，葬禮依盧魯元故事。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously granted Prince of Taiyuan, posthumous title Kang; funeral rites followed Lu Luyuan's precedent.
translations.idiomatic: At death he was posthumously Prince of Taiyuan, styled Kang; funeral rites followed Luyuan's precedent.

sentences.zh: 太和初，子倪襲爵。

translations.literal: At the start of Taihe his son Ni inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: At Taihe's start his son Ni inherited.

sentences.zh: 萬安國，代人也。

translations.literal: Wan Anguo was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Anguo was a man of Dai.

sentences.zh: 世為酋帥。

translations.literal: For generations his house were tribal chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: His line were chiefs for generations.

sentences.zh: 父振，尚高陽長公主，拜駙馬都尉，位長安鎮將，爵馮翊公。

translations.literal: His father Zhen married the Princess of Gaoyang and was Commandant of the Horse Guards Consort, held as Chang'an Garrison Commander, title Duke of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhen married the Princess of Gaoyang, was Commandant of the Horse Guards Consort, Chang'an Garrison Commander, Duke of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 安國少明敏，以國甥復尚河南公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Anguo was clever and keen in youth; as the emperor's sister's son he again married the Princess of Henan and was Commandant of the Horse Guards Consort.
translations.idiomatic: Clever in youth, as imperial nephew he again married the Princess of Henan and became Commandant of the Horse Guards Consort.

sentences.zh: 獻文特親寵之，與同臥起。

translations.literal: Xianwen especially favored him, sharing bed and rising.
translations.idiomatic: Xianwen favored him especially — they shared bed and rising.

sentences.zh: 拜大司馬、大將軍，封安城王。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Marshal, Grand General, and enfeoffed Prince of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Marshal, Grand General, and Prince of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 安國先與神部長奚買奴不平，承明初，矯詔殺買奴于苑中。

translations.literal: Anguo had earlier been at odds with Divine Tribe chief Xi Mainu; at the start of Chenming he forged an edict and killed Mainu in the park.
translations.idiomatic: He had quarreled with Divine Tribe chief Xi Mainu; in Chenming's start he forged an edict and killed Mainu in the park.

sentences.zh: 孝文聞之，大怒，遂賜死，年二十三。

translations.literal: When Xiaowen heard, he was greatly angry and had him ordered to die; he was twenty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen heard and was furious; he was ordered to die at twenty-three.

sentences.zh: 子翼襲王爵。

translations.literal: His son Yi inherited the princely title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi inherited the princely title.

sentences.zh: 有嵇根者，世為紇奚部帥。

translations.literal: There was one Ji Gen, for generations chief of the Xi tribe.
translations.idiomatic: One Ji Gen, for generations chief of the Xi tribe.

sentences.zh: 皇始初，率部歸魏，尚昭成女。

translations.literal: At the start of Huangshi he led his tribe to submit to Wei and married a daughter of Zhaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: At Huangshi's start he led his tribe to Wei and married Zhaocheng's daughter.

sentences.zh: 生子拔，位尚書令。

translations.literal: He begot a son Ba, who held Minister Director.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ba held Minister Director.

sentences.zh: 拔尚華陰公主，生子敬。

translations.literal: Ba married the Princess of Huayin and begot a son Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Ba married the Princess of Huayin and begot Jing.

sentences.zh: 元紹之逆也，主有功，超授敬大司馬，封長樂王。

translations.literal: In Yuan Shao's rebellion the princess had merit; Jing was exceptionally appointed Grand Marshal and enfeoffed Prince of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuan Shao's rebellion the princess had merit; Jing was raised to Grand Marshal and Prince of Changle.

sentences.zh: 薨，子護襲，拜外都大官。

translations.literal: He died; his son Hu inherited and was appointed Outer Palace Grand Provisioner.
translations.idiomatic: He died; son Hu inherited and was Outer Palace Grand Provisioner.

sentences.zh: 根事蹟遺落，故略附云。

translations.literal: Gen's deeds were lost; therefore this brief note is appended.
translations.idiomatic: Gen's deeds are lost; hence this brief note.

sentences.zh: 周觀，代人也，驍勇有膂力。

translations.literal: Zhou Guan was a man of Dai, fierce and brave with bodily strength.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Guan of Dai was fierce, brave, and strong.

sentences.zh: 太武以軍功賜爵金城公，位高平鎮將。

translations.literal: Taiwu for military merit granted Duke of Jincheng and made him Garrison Commander of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: For merit Taiwu made him Duke of Jincheng and Garrison Commander of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 善撫士卒，號有威名。

translations.literal: Skilled at comforting soldiers, he was styled to have a formidable name.
translations.idiomatic: He comforted troops well and won a name for awe.

sentences.zh: 後拜內都大官，出為秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Inner Palace Grand Provisioner and went out as Governor of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later Inner Palace Grand Provisioner, then Governor of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 撫馭失和，部人薛永宗聚眾汾曲以叛。

translations.literal: His governing lost harmony; tribesman Xue Yongzong gathered a crowd in the Fen bend and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Governing poorly, tribesman Xue Yongzong gathered men in the Fen bend and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 觀討永宗，為流矢所中。

translations.literal: Guan attacked Yongzong and was struck by a stray arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Guan attacked Yongzong and was hit by a stray arrow.

sentences.zh: 太武幸蒲阪，觀聞帝至，驚怖而起，瘡重遂卒。

translations.literal: Taiwu visited Puban; Guan heard the emperor had come, rose in fright, his wound worsened, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu came to Puban; Guan heard, started up in fright, his wound worsened, and he died.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，絕其爵云。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and stripped his title.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and stripped his title.

sentences.zh: 子延，字契胡提，頗有氣幹。

translations.literal: His son Yan, styled Qihuti, had considerable force of character.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan, styled Qihuti, had real backbone.

sentences.zh: 襲爵河南公，例降，改封汝陽侯。

translations.literal: He inherited Duke of Henan; by precedent the title was reduced and he was re-enfeoffed Marquis of Ruyang.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited Duke of Henan; by rule it was lowered to Marquis of Ruyang.

sentences.zh: 位懷朔鎮大將、太僕卿。

translations.literal: He held Great General of Huaishuo Garrison and Minister of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He was Great General of Huaishuo Garrison and Minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 受使綏慰秀容，為牧子所害

translations.literal: Sent to soothe Xiurong, he was killed by herdsmen.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to pacify Xiurong, he was killed by herdsmen.

sentences.zh: 呂洛拔，代人也。

translations.literal: Lu Luoba was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Luoba was a man of Dai.

sentences.zh: 曾祖渴侯，昭成時率戶五千歸魏。

translations.literal: Great-grandfather Kehou in Zhaocheng's time led five thousand households to submit to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandfather Kehou in Zhaocheng's time led five thousand households to Wei.

sentences.zh: 父匹知，太武時為西部長，封榮陽公。

translations.literal: His father Pizhi in Taiwu's time was western tribal chief and enfeoffed Duke of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Pizhi under Taiwu was western tribal chief, Duke of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 洛拔以壯勇知名。

translations.literal: Luoba was known for stalwart courage.
translations.idiomatic: Luoba was known for courage.

sentences.zh: 文成末，為平原鎮都將。

translations.literal: At the end of Wencheng he was Chief Commander of Pingyuan Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: At Wencheng's end he was Chief Commander of Pingyuan Garrison.

sentences.zh: 隨尉元攻宋將張永，大敗之，賜爵成武侯。

translations.literal: Following Wei Yuan attacking Song general Zhang Yong, he routed him greatly and was granted Marquis of Chengwu.
translations.idiomatic: With Wei Yuan against Song's Zhang Yong he won a great rout and was made Marquis of Chengwu.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 長子文祖，獻文以其勳臣子，補龍牧曹奏事中散。

translations.literal: Eldest son Wenzu — Xianwen, because he was a meritorious minister's son, made him supplemental Dragon Herds Office Memorial Drafter and Central Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest son Wenzu — Xianwen, as a hero's son, made him supplemental Memorial Drafter in the Dragon Herds Office and Central Attendant.

sentences.zh: 以牧產不滋，坐徙武川鎮。

translations.literal: Because herds did not thrive he was demoted to Wuchuan Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When herds failed to thrive he was sent to Wuchuan Garrison.

sentences.zh: 後文祖以舊語譯注皇誥，辭義通辯，為外都曹奏事中散。

translations.literal: Later Wenzu translated and annotated the imperial pronouncements in the old tongue; his wording was fluent and clear, and he was Memorial Drafter in the Outer Office.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wenzu translated the imperial edicts in the old tongue with fluent clarity and became Outer Office Memorial Drafter.

sentences.zh: 後坐事伏法。

translations.literal: Later he was executed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was executed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 薛彪子，代人也。

translations.literal: Xue Biaozi was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Biaozi was a man of Dai.

sentences.zh: 祖達頭，自姚萇時率部落歸魏。

translations.literal: Grandfather Datou from Yao Chang's time led the tribe to submit to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Datou in Yao Chang's time led the tribe to Wei.

sentences.zh: 道武賜爵聊城侯，待以上客禮，賜妻鄭氏。

translations.literal: Daowu granted Marquis of Liaocheng and treated him with honored-guest rites, giving Lady Zheng in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu made him Marquis of Liaocheng, treated him as honored guest, and gave him Lady Zheng.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈冀州刺史，諡曰悼。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously granted Governor of Jizhou, posthumous title Mournful.
translations.idiomatic: At death posthumously Governor of Jizhou, styled Mournful.

sentences.zh: 父野潆者，並、太二州刺史，封河東公，有聲稱。

translations.literal: His father Yeying was Governor of Bing and Tai, enfeoffed Duke of Hedong, with a sounding reputation.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yeying was Governor of Bing and Tai, Duke of Hedong, well spoken of.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Simple.
translations.idiomatic: He died, styled Simple.

sentences.zh: 彪子姿貌壯偉，明斷有父風。

translations.literal: Biaozi was imposing in appearance, clear in judgment, with his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Biaozi was imposing, clear-judging, his father's son.

sentences.zh: 為內行長，典奏諸曹事。

translations.literal: He was Inner Conduct Director, overseeing memorial affairs of the various offices.
translations.idiomatic: He was Inner Conduct Director, overseeing the offices' memorials.

sentences.zh: 當官正直，內外憚之。

translations.literal: Upright in office, within and without they feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Upright in office — all feared him.

sentences.zh: 及文明太后臨朝，出為枋頭鎮將。
