translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Wenming held court, he went out as Garrison Commander of Fangtou.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Wenming ruled, he went out as Fangtou Garrison Commander.

sentences.zh: 素剛簡，為近臣所嫉；

translations.literal: By nature stern and simple, he was envied by near ministers;
translations.idiomatic: Stern and plain by nature, near ministers envied him;

sentences.zh: 因小過，黜為鎮門士。

translations.literal: for a small fault he was demoted to garrison gate guard.
translations.idiomatic: for a small fault he was reduced to garrison gate guard.

sentences.zh: 及獻文南巡，次山陽，彪子拜訴于路，復除枋頭鎮將。

translations.literal: When Xianwen toured south and halted at Shanyang, Biaozi appealed on the road and was again appointed Fangtou Garrison Commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianwen went south and stopped at Shanyang, Biaozi appealed on the road and was again Fangtou commander.

sentences.zh: 累遷開府、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted Opening Office and Governor of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Opening Office and Governor of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 在州甚多惠政，百姓便之。

translations.literal: In the province he had many benevolent policies; the people found him convenient.
translations.idiomatic: In the province he ruled with mercy; the people were at ease.

sentences.zh: 沛郡太守邵安、下邳太守張攀，咸以贓汙，彪子案之於法。

translations.literal: Pei commandery Administrator Shao An and Xiapi Administrator Zhang Pan were both corrupt; Biaozi prosecuted them by law.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Administrator Shao An and Xiapi Administrator Zhang Pan were corrupt; Biaozi tried them by law.

sentences.zh: 安等遣子弟上書，誣彪子南通賊虜。

translations.literal: An and the rest sent younger brothers to memorialize, falsely accusing Biaozi of secretly communicating with southern bandits.
translations.idiomatic: They sent younger kin to accuse Biaozi of secretly aiding southern bandits.

sentences.zh: 孝文曰：「此妄矣。

translations.literal: Xiaowen said: "This is false."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen said, "This is nonsense."

sentences.zh: 」推案果虛。

translations.literal: Investigation proved it empty.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation proved it empty.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰文。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Literary.
translations.idiomatic: He died, styled Literary.

sentences.zh: 子琡。

translations.literal: His son Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhu.

sentences.zh: 琡字曇珍，形貌瑰偉。

translations.literal: Zhu, styled Tanzhen, was striking in form and appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu, styled Tanzhen, was striking to look upon.

sentences.zh: 少以幹用為典客令。

translations.literal: In youth for capability he was made Director of Guests.
translations.idiomatic: Young, capable, he was made Director of Guests.

sentences.zh: 每引見，儀望甚美。

translations.literal: Whenever summoned to audience his bearing was very fine.
translations.idiomatic: Each audience found his bearing fine.

sentences.zh: 宣武謂曰：「卿風度峻整，姿貌秀異，後當升進，何以處官？

translations.literal: Xuanwu said to him: "Your manner is stern and whole, your appearance outstanding — you will rise later; how do you see your office?"
translations.idiomatic: Xuanwu said, "Your bearing is whole, your looks outstanding — you will rise; how do you see your post?"

sentences.zh: 」琡答曰：「宗廟之禮，不敢不敬；

translations.literal: Zhu answered: "In ancestral temple rites I dare not fail in reverence;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu answered, "In ancestral rites I dare not fail in reverence;

sentences.zh: 朝廷之事，不敢不忠。

translations.literal: in court affairs I dare not fail in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: in court affairs I dare not fail in loyalty.

sentences.zh: 自此之外，非庸臣所及。

translations.literal: Beyond this, it is not for a mediocre minister to reach."
translations.idiomatic: Beyond that, a mediocre minister cannot reach."

sentences.zh: 」正光中，行洛陽令，部內肅然。

translations.literal: In Zhengguang he acted as Magistrate of Luoyang; within his district all was orderly.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengguang he acted Luoyang Magistrate; the district was orderly.

sentences.zh: 時以久旱，京師見囚悉召集於都亭，理問冤滯。

translations.literal: Because of long drought, capital prisoners were all gathered at the capital pavilion to examine delayed wrongs.
translations.idiomatic: In long drought, capital prisoners were gathered at the capital pavilion to clear delayed wrongs.

sentences.zh: 洛陽獄唯有三人。

translations.literal: Luoyang's prison held only three men.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang's prison held only three men.

sentences.zh: 孝明嘉之，賜縑百疋。

translations.literal: Xiaoming commended this and granted a hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoming praised this and gave a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 琡本附元叉，叉廢，憂懼，由是政教廢弛，坐免官。

translations.literal: Zhu had earlier attached to Yuan Cha; when Cha was deposed he was anxious and fearful — from this governance and teaching slackened, and he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu had clung to Yuan Cha; when Cha fell he was afraid — rule slackened and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 李神軌有寵于靈太后，琡復事之。

translations.literal: Li Shengui had favor with Empress Dowager Ling; Zhu again served him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shengui had Ling Empress Dowager's favor; Zhu served him again.

sentences.zh: 累遷吏部郎中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Bureau Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Bureau Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 先是，吏部尚書崔亮奏立停年格，不簡人才，專問勞舊。

translations.literal: Earlier, Minister of Personnel Cui Liang had memorialized establishing the seniority-stop rule, not sorting talent, asking only seniority and old service.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Minister Cui Liang had proposed the seniority-stop rule — no sorting by talent, only years and old service.

sentences.zh: 琡乃上書曰：「臣聞錦縠雖輕，不委之以學割；

translations.literal: Zhu then submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that though brocade is light, one does not entrust learning to cut with it;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu memorialized: "I hear that though brocade is light, one does not use it to learn cutting;

sentences.zh: 瑚璉任重，豈寄之以弱力。

translations.literal: though ritual vessels are heavy, one cannot entrust them to weak strength.
translations.idiomatic: though ritual vessels are heavy, one does not set them on weak shoulders.

sentences.zh: 若使選曹唯取年勞，不簡賢否，使義均行雁。

translations.literal: If the selection office takes only years of service and does not sort worthy from unworthy, it makes righteousness equal to flying geese in line.
translations.idiomatic: If selection takes only seniority, not worth, it makes merit a line of geese.

sentences.zh: 次若貫魚，勘簿呼名，一吏足矣。

translations.literal: Next, strung like fish on a skewer, checking registers and calling names — one clerk suffices.
translations.idiomatic: Strung like fish on a skewer, one clerk calling names from the register suffices.

sentences.zh: 數人而用，何謂銓衡？

translations.literal: What then is the meaning of weighing and balancing?"
translations.idiomatic: Why then keep a Ministry of Personnel?"

sentences.zh: 今黎元之命系於守長。

translations.literal: Now the people's lives hang on prefects and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Now the people's lives hang on prefects and magistrates.

sentences.zh: 若其得人，則蘇息有地；

translations.literal: If they get the right men, there is ground for revival;
translations.idiomatic: If the right men are found, the land can breathe again;

sentences.zh: 任非其器，為患更深。

translations.literal: if the wrong men are set in office, the harm goes deeper.
translations.idiomatic: if the wrong men are set, harm runs deeper.

sentences.zh: 請郡縣之職，吏部先盡擇才，並學通古今曉達政職者，以應其選。

translations.literal: Your servant asks that commandery and county posts — the Ministry first choose talent throughout, all who have mastered classics and histories and understand governing — to meet selection.
translations.idiomatic: Let commandery and county posts be filled first from talent who know classics, histories, and rule.

sentences.zh: 不拘入職遠近，年勳多少，其積勞之中，有才堪牧人者，自在先用之限。

translations.literal: Not bound by distance of entry, amount of years or merit — among accumulated service, any with talent fit to shepherd people should stand within the first-use limit.
translations.idiomatic: Do not bind by years alone; among the long-serving, any fit to govern should be used first.

sentences.zh: 其餘不堪者，既壯藉其力，豈容老而棄之。

translations.literal: The rest unfit — now in their prime you borrow their strength; how can you cast them off in old age?"
translations.idiomatic: The rest, unfit but still strong — how cast them off when old?"

sentences.zh: 將佐丞尉去人稍遠，小小當否，未為多失，宜依次補敘，以酬其勞。

translations.literal: Adjutants, aides, assistants, and commandants are somewhat farther from the people; small right and wrong are not great loss — they should be filled in order to repay their labor."
translations.idiomatic: Deputies and aides are farther from the people; small errors matter less — fill them in order to repay labor."

sentences.zh: 」書奏，不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; no reply.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went in; no reply.

sentences.zh: 後因引見，復陳之曰：「今四方初定，務在養人。

translations.literal: Later on being summoned to audience he again stated: "Now the four quarters are newly settled; the task is to nurture the people.
translations.idiomatic: Later at audience he said again, "The realm is newly settled; the task is to nurture the people.

sentences.zh: 臣請依漢氏更立四科，令三公宰貴各薦時賢，以補郡縣。

translations.literal: Your servant asks to follow Han precedent and newly establish four categories, ordering the Three Dukes and noble ministers each to recommend men of the time to supplement commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: I ask to follow Han and renew the four categories, letting Three Dukes and nobles each recommend talent for commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 明立條格，防其阿黨之端。

translations.literal: Clearly set rules to guard against factions.
translations.idiomatic: Set clear rules against factions.

sentences.zh: 庶令塗炭之余，戴仰有地。

translations.literal: Perhaps then the people in ashes and charcoal may have ground to look up."
translations.idiomatic: Then perhaps those in ashes may have something to look up to."

sentences.zh: 」詔下公卿議之，事亦寢。

translations.literal: An edict was sent down to the Three Dukes and ministers for discussion; the matter also lay dormant.
translations.idiomatic: An edict went to the Three Dukes for discussion; the matter also died.

sentences.zh: 元天穆討邢杲，以琡為行台尚書。

translations.literal: Yuan Tianmu campaigned against Xing Guo and made Zhu Mobile-Office Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tianmu campaigned against Xing Guo and made Zhu Mobile-Office Minister.

sentences.zh: 軍次東郡，時元顥已據贊阝城，邢杲又逼曆下，天穆議其所先。

translations.literal: The army halted at Dongjun; then Yuan Hao had already seized Zancheng, and Xing Guo also pressed Lixia; Tianmu debated which to strike first.
translations.idiomatic: The army stopped at Dongjun; Yuan Hao held Zancheng, Xing Guo pressed Lixia; Tianmu debated priority.

sentences.zh: 議者咸以杲盛，宜先經略。

translations.literal: Discussants all said Guo was strong and the border should be taken first.
translations.idiomatic: All said Guo was strong and the border should come first.

sentences.zh: 唯琡以杲為聚眾無名，雖強猶賊。

translations.literal: Only Zhu held that Guo was a mob without a name — though strong, still a bandit.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zhu said Guo was a nameless mob — strong, but still bandits.

sentences.zh: 元顥皇室昵親，來稱義舉。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao was the imperial clan's close kin, coming in the name of righteous rising.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao was imperial kin, coming under the banner of righteous rising.

sentences.zh: 自河陰之役，人情駭怨，今有際會，易生感動。

translations.literal: Since the battle at Heyin the people's hearts were shocked and resentful; now there is a chance — easy to stir feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Since Heyin hearts were shocked; now a chance stirs them easily.

sentences.zh: 待顥事決，然後回師。

translations.literal: Wait until Hao's affair is settled, then turn the army.
translations.idiomatic: Settle Hao first, then turn the army.

sentences.zh: 天穆以群情所願，遂先討杲。

translations.literal: Tianmu followed the crowd's wish and first attacked Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Tianmu followed the crowd and struck Guo first.

sentences.zh: 杲降，軍還至定陶，天穆留琡行西兗州事。

translations.literal: Guo surrendered; the army returned to Dingtao; Tianmu left Zhu to act for Western Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guo surrendered; returning to Dingtao, Tianmu left Zhu acting for Western Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋為元顥所陷。

translations.literal: Soon he was trapped by Yuan Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was trapped by Yuan Hao.

sentences.zh: 顥執琡自隨。

translations.literal: Hao seized Zhu and kept him with him.
translations.idiomatic: Hao seized Zhu and kept him at his side.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮破顥，天穆謂琡曰：「不用君言，乃至於此！」

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong broke Hao; Tianmu said to Zhu: "Had we not used your words, it would have come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong broke Hao; Tianmu told Zhu, "Had we heeded you, we would not be here!"

sentences.zh: 天平初，拜七兵尚書。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianping he was appointed Minister of the Seven Arms.
translations.idiomatic: At Tianping's start he was Minister of the Seven Arms.

sentences.zh: 齊神武引為丞相府長史，軍國之事，多所關知。

translations.literal: Qi Shenwu drew him as Chief Clerk of the Chancellor's Office; military and state affairs he knew much of.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shenwu made him Chief Clerk; he knew much of army and state.

sentences.zh: 叔亦推誠盡節，屢進忠讜。

translations.literal: Zhu also pushed sincerity to the limit, repeatedly offering loyal remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu too gave full sincerity, offering loyal remonstrance again and again.

sentences.zh: 神武大舉西伐，將度蒲津。

translations.literal: Shenwu made a great western campaign and was about to cross the Pu ford.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu marched west in force and was about to cross the Pu ford.

sentences.zh: 琡諫曰：「西賊連年饑饉，故冒死來入陝州。

translations.literal: Zhu remonstrated: "Western bandits have suffered famine for years; therefore they risk death to enter Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu urged: "Western foes have starved for years; they risk death to enter Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 但宜置兵諸道，勿與野戰。

translations.literal: Only place troops on every road and do not meet them in field battle.
translations.idiomatic: Only post troops on every road; do not fight in the open.

sentences.zh: 比及來年麥秋，人應餓死，寶炬、黑獺自然歸降。

translations.literal: By next year's wheat harvest people should starve to death; Bao Ju and Hei Da will naturally submit.
translations.idiomatic: By next harvest they will starve; Bao Ju and Hei Da will submit of themselves.

sentences.zh: 願無渡河。

translations.literal: I beg you not to cross the river."
translations.idiomatic: I beg you not to cross the river."

sentences.zh: 」侯景亦曰：「今舉兵極大，萬不一捷，卒難收斂。

translations.literal: Hou Jing also said: "Now the army raised is at its utmost; ten thousand in one will not succeed — hard to gather in at the end.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing also said, "This army is raised to the limit; one chance in ten thousand — hard to pull back.

sentences.zh: 不如分為二軍，相繼而進，前軍若勝，後軍合力；

translations.literal: Better divide into two armies and advance in succession; if the first wins, the second joins force;
translations.idiomatic: Better split into two armies in succession; if the first wins, the second adds force;

sentences.zh: 前軍若敗，後軍承之。

translations.literal: if the first loses, the second takes it up."
translations.idiomatic: if the first loses, the second takes it up."

sentences.zh: 」神武皆弗納，遂有沙苑之敗。

translations.literal: Shenwu accepted neither and thus had the defeat at Shayuan.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu took neither counsel and met defeat at Shayuan.

sentences.zh: 後范陽盧仲禮反，琡與諸軍討平之。

translations.literal: Later Fanyang Lu Zhongli rebelled; Zhu with the various armies pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lu Zhongli of Fanyang rebelled; Zhu with other armies pacified him.

sentences.zh: 轉殷州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred Governor of Yinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred Governor of Yinzhou.

sentences.zh: 為政嚴酷，吏人苦之。

translations.literal: His governance was harsh; officials and people suffered.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled harshly; officials and people suffered.

sentences.zh: 後歷位度支、殿中二尚書。

translations.literal: Later he held in succession the two ministries of Revenue and Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Later he held the ministries of Revenue and Palace in turn.

sentences.zh: 天保元年，卒于兼尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao he died while Acting Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao year one he died as Acting Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 臨終，敕其子斂以時服。

translations.literal: At the end he charged his sons to bury him in timely dress.
translations.idiomatic: Dying, he ordered his sons to bury him in plain timely dress.

sentences.zh: 逾月便葬，不聽幹求贈官。

translations.literal: Within a month he was buried; pleas for posthumous offices were not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried within the month; no posthumous offices were granted despite entreaties.

sentences.zh: 自製喪車，不加雕飾，但用麻為旒蘇，繩網路而已。

translations.literal: He had his own mourning carriage made without carved ornament—only hemp tassels and cord netting.
translations.idiomatic: He designed his own hearse: no carving, only hemp tassels and rope mesh.

sentences.zh: 明器等物，並不令置。

translations.literal: Bright vessels and the like were not permitted at all.
translations.idiomatic: Grave goods and bright vessels were forbidden entirely.

sentences.zh: 琡久在省闥，明閑簿領，當官剖斷，敏速如流。

translations.literal: Yu had long served in the central offices, skilled in records and registers; in office he judged cases, swift as flowing water.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had long served in the capital, expert in ledgers and registers; on the bench his rulings ran swift as water.

sentences.zh: 然天性險忌，情義不篤。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was treacherous and jealous, shallow in friendship and duty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was treacherous and jealous by nature, shallow in friendship and loyalty.

sentences.zh: 外若方格，內實浮動。

translations.literal: Outwardly he seemed square and ruled; inwardly he was inconstant.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly he looked square and stern; inwardly he was restless.

sentences.zh: 受納貨賄，曲理舞法，深文刻薄，多所傷害。

translations.literal: He accepted bribes, bent reason and twisted law, harsh in wording and cruel—many were harmed.
translations.idiomatic: He took bribes, bent law to favor, piled on harsh charges—many were ruined.

sentences.zh: 人士畏惡之。

translations.literal: Gentlemen feared and hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Men of standing feared and loathed him.

sentences.zh: 魏東平王元匡妾張氏，淫逸放恣。

translations.literal: Lady Zhang, concubine of Prince of Dongping Yuan Kuang of Wei, was dissolute and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang, concubine to Wei's Prince of Dongping Yuan Kuang, was wanton and unbridled.

sentences.zh: 琡初與奸通，後納以為婦。

translations.literal: Yu at first committed adultery with her, then took her as wife.
translations.idiomatic: Yu first lay with her in secret, then made her his wife.

sentences.zh: 惑其讒言，遂棄前妻于氏，不忍其子允。

translations.literal: Beguiled by her slanders, he cast off his former wife of the Yu clan, unwilling toward his son Yun.
translations.idiomatic: He heeded her slanders, cast off his first wife of the Yu house, and turned cold to his son Yun.

sentences.zh: 家人內忿，競相告列，深為世所譏鄙。

translations.literal: The household seethed within; they reported one another in rivalry, and he was deeply scorned by the world.
translations.idiomatic: His kin seethed and denounced one another; the world held him in deep contempt.

sentences.zh: 贈開府儀同三司、尚書左僕射、青州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Opening the Government with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted Opening the Government with Three Excellencies' ceremonial rank, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Qing.

sentences.zh: 諡曰威恭。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Majestic and Reverent.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous title: Majestic and Reverent.

sentences.zh: 子允嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yun succeeded.

sentences.zh: 尉元，字苟仁，代人也。

translations.literal: Wei Yuan, styled Gourou, was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuan, styled Gourou, came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 世為豪宗。

translations.literal: For generations his house was a great clan.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had been a great house for generations.

sentences.zh: 父目斤，勇略聞於當時，位中山太守。

translations.literal: His father Mukin was famed in his day for courage and strategy and held the post of Administrator of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mukin was famed for courage and stratagem and served as Administrator of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 元以善射稱，為羽林中郎，以匪懈見知。

translations.literal: Yuan was famed for skill in archery and was made Gentleman of the Feathered Forest; for tireless diligence he won notice.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was known for archery and made Gentleman of the Feathered Forest; tireless service won him notice.

sentences.zh: 稍遷駕部給事中，賜爵富城男。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Master of Carriages attendant and enfeoffed Baron of Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Master of Carriages attendant and was enfeoffed Baron of Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 和平中，遷北部尚書，進爵太昌侯。

translations.literal: In the Heping era he was transferred to Northern Minister of the Imperial Clan and advanced to Marquis of Taichang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Heping era he became Northern Minister of the Imperial Clan and was advanced to Marquis of Taichang.

sentences.zh: 天安元年，薛安都以徐州內附，獻文以元為持節、都督東道諸軍事，與城陽公孔伯恭赴之。

translations.literal: In Tian'an year 1, Xue Andu of Song surrendered Xu Province to the court; Emperor Xiaowen made Yuan bearer of the staff of authority and commander of military affairs on the eastern route, and he went with Duke of Chengyang Kong Bogong.
translations.idiomatic: In Tian'an 1 Xue Andu of Song surrendered Xu Province; Emperor Xiaowen made Yuan bearer of the staff and eastern-route commander, and he set out with Duke of Chengyang Kong Bogong.

sentences.zh: 宋兗州刺史畢眾敬遣東平太守章仇舣歸款，元並納之，遂長驅而進。

translations.literal: Bi Zhongjing, Governor of Yan Province in Song, sent Administrator of Dongping Zhang Chouyi to submit; Yuan received them all and drove forward at length.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Zhongjing, Song's Governor of Yan, sent Dongping's administrator Zhang Chouyi to submit; Yuan took them in and pressed on at length.

sentences.zh: 宋遣將張永、沈攸之等屯于下鹈蓋。

translations.literal: Song sent generals Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi and others to encamp at the approaches to Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Song sent Zhang Yong, Shen Youzhi, and others to camp at the Xiapi approaches.

sentences.zh: 安都出城見元。

translations.literal: Andu came out of the city to see Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Andu came out of the city to meet Yuan.

sentences.zh: 元依朝旨，授其徐州刺史，遣中書侍郎高閭、李璨等與安都俱還入城。

translations.literal: Yuan, following court orders, appointed him Governor of Xu Province and sent Secretariat Attendant Gao Lu, Li Can, and others back into the city with Andu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, per the court's order, made Andu Governor of Xu and sent Secretariat Attendants Gao Lu and Li Can into the city with him.

sentences.zh: 別令孔伯恭撫安內外，然後元入彭城。

translations.literal: He separately ordered Kong Bogong to reassure Andu inside and out, and only then did Yuan enter Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He left Kong Bogong to steady Andu within and without, then entered Pengcheng himself.

sentences.zh: 元以永仍據險要，乃命安都與璨等同守。

translations.literal: Because Yong still held strategic ground, Yuan ordered Andu and Can to defend together.
translations.idiomatic: Yong still held the choke points, so Yuan had Andu and Can hold the city together.

sentences.zh: 身率精銳，揚兵於外，分擊呂梁，絕其糧運。

translations.literal: He himself led crack troops, raised banners without, struck Liangcheng in divisions, and cut their grain route.
translations.idiomatic: He led picked troops abroad, struck Liangcheng in detachments, and severed their grain line.

sentences.zh: 永遂捐城夜遁。

translations.literal: Yong thereupon abandoned the city and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Yong abandoned the city and fled by night.

sentences.zh: 於是遣高閭與張讜對為東徐州刺史；

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Gao Lu and Zhang Tan as paired Governors of Eastern Xu Province;
translations.idiomatic: He then paired Gao Lu with Zhang Tan as Governors of Eastern Xu;

sentences.zh: 李璨與畢眾敬對為東兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Li Can and Bi Zhongjing as paired Governors of Eastern Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: and Li Can with Bi Zhongjing as Governors of Eastern Yan.

sentences.zh: 拜元開府、都督、徐州刺史、淮陽公。

translations.literal: Yuan was appointed Opening the Government, Commander-in-Chief, Governor of Xu Province, and Duke of Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was made Opening the Government, Commander-in-Chief, Governor of Xu, and Duke of Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 太和初，徵為內都大官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe he was summoned as Grand Steward of the Inner Court.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Taihe he was summoned as Grand Steward of the Inner Court.

sentences.zh: 既而出為使持節、鎮西大將軍、開府、統萬鎮都將，甚得夷人之心。

translations.literal: Shortly after he went out as bearer of the staff, Grand General Who Guards the West, Opening the Government, and Commander-in-Chief at Tongwan—he won the hearts of the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he went out as bearer of the staff, Grand General Who Guards the West, Opening the Government, and commander at Tongwan, and won the tribes' hearts.

sentences.zh: 三年，進爵淮陽王，以舊老見禮，聽乘步挽，杖於朝。

translations.literal: In year 3 he was advanced to Prince of Huaiyang; as an elder of long standing he was honored, permitted a palanquin and staff in court.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he was made Prince of Huaiyang; as a veteran he was honored with a palanquin and staff at court.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝既立，多遣間諜，扇動新人；

translations.literal: After Emperor Gao of Qi was established, he sent many spies to stir the newly submitted;
translations.idiomatic: After Gao of Qi took the throne, he sent spies to stir the new subjects;

sentences.zh: 不逞之徒，所在蜂起。

translations.literal: malcontents rose everywhere like wasps.
translations.idiomatic: and malcontents swarmed up everywhere.

sentences.zh: 以元威名夙振，使總率諸軍以討之。

translations.literal: Because Yuan's prestige had long resounded, he was sent to command all armies to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's name had long carried; he was sent to command all armies against them.

sentences.zh: 東南清晏，遠近帖然。

translations.literal: The southeast was pacified; far and near submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The southeast was cleared; far and near lay quiet.

sentences.zh: 入為侍中、都曹尚書，遷尚書令，進位司徒。

translations.literal: He entered as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Department of State Affairs, transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing, and advanced to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He entered as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Department of State Affairs, became Director of the Masters of Writing, and rose to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 十年，例降庶姓王爵，封山陽郡公。

translations.literal: In year 10, by precedent the princely surname was reduced to commoner rank; he was enfeoffed Duke of Shanyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10, by precedent princely houses were reduced to common rank; he was enfeoffed Duke of Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 其年，頻表以老乞身，詔許之。

translations.literal: That year he repeatedly memorialized that age compelled retirement; the edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: That year he repeatedly begged to retire on account of age; the edict allowed it.

sentences.zh: 元詣闕謝老，引見於庭；

translations.literal: Yuan came to court to thank him for release and was received in the hall;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan came to court to thank the emperor for release and was received in the hall;

sentences.zh: 命升殿勞宴，賜玄冠、素服。

translations.literal: ordered to ascend the hall for a feast of honor; granted a dark cap and plain robes.
translations.idiomatic: ordered up the hall for a feast of honor and given a dark cap and plain robes.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「前司徒山陽郡公尉元、前大鴻臚卿新泰伯游明根，並元亨利貞，明允誠素，位顯台宿，歸老私第。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "Former Minister of Works Wei Yuan, Duke of Shanyang Commandery, and former Grand Herald You Minggen, Marquis of Xintai—both possess the four virtues of the Changes, bright trust and plain sincerity, ranks eminent at the terrace stars, returning in old age to private dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict read: "Former Minister of Works Wei Yuan of Shanyang and former Grand Herald You Minggen of Xintai—both embody the four virtues of the Changes, bright in trust and plain in heart, eminent at court, now retiring to their homes.

sentences.zh: 可謂知始知卒，希世之賢也。

translations.literal: They may be called to know the beginning and know the end—worthies rare in an age."
translations.idiomatic: They know the start and the finish—worthies rare in their time."

sentences.zh: 公以八十之年，宜處三老之重；

translations.literal: Sir, at eighty years, should occupy the weight of the three elders;
translations.idiomatic: Sir, at eighty, should bear the weight of the three elders;

sentences.zh: 卿以七十之齡，可充五更之選。

translations.literal: Minister, at seventy years, may fill the choice of the five elders."
translations.idiomatic: Minister, at seventy, may serve among the five elders."

sentences.zh: 」於是養三老、五更於明堂，國老、庶老於階下。

translations.literal: Thereupon the three elders and five elders were nurtured in the Bright Hall, the state elders and common elders on the steps below.
translations.idiomatic: Then the three elders and five elders were honored in the Bright Hall, state and common elders on the steps below.

sentences.zh: 孝文再拜三老，親袒割牲，執爵而饋；

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen bowed twice to the three elders, bared his shoulder and cut the victim himself, held the cup and fed them;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen bowed twice to the three elders, bared shoulder and cut the victim himself, held the cup and fed them;

sentences.zh: 於五更行肅拜之禮；

translations.literal: toward the five elders he performed the bow of respect;
translations.idiomatic: to the five elders he performed the bow of respect;

sentences.zh: 賜國老、庶老衣服有差。

translations.literal: robes were granted to state elders and common elders in graded measure.
translations.idiomatic: robes were granted to state and common elders by rank.

sentences.zh: 既而元言曰：「自天地分判，五行施則，人之所崇，莫重于孝順。

translations.literal: Then Yuan said: "Since heaven and earth were divided and the Five Agents operated their laws, what men revere—none is weightier than filial obedience.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan then said: "Since heaven and earth split and the Five Agents ran their course, nothing men honor weighs more than filial piety.

sentences.zh: 然五孝六順，天下之所先，願陛下重之，以化四方。

translations.literal: Yet the five filial acts and six harmonies are what the realm puts first; I pray Your Majesty will weight them to transform the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The five filial acts and six harmonies lead the realm; I pray Your Majesty will weight them to transform the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 臣既年衰，不究遠趣，心耳所及，敢不盡誠。

translations.literal: I am already aged and do not probe distant ends; what heart and ear reach, I dare not withhold sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: I am old and cannot see far; what heart and ear reach, I dare not withhold truth.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「孝順之道，天地之經。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The way of filial obedience is the warp of heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Filial obedience is the warp of heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 今承三老明言，銘之於懷。

translations.literal: Now receiving the three elders' clear words, I inscribe them in my breast."
translations.idiomatic: Now I receive the three elders' clear words and inscribe them in my breast."

sentences.zh: 」明根言曰：「夫至孝通靈，至順感幽，故《詩》云：'孝悌之至，通於神明，光于四海。

translations.literal: Minggen said: "Utmost filial piety penetrates spirits; utmost harmony moves the unseen—hence the Odes: 'When filial piety and fraternal duty reach their height, they communicate with spirits and gods and shine across the four seas.'
translations.idiomatic: Minggen said: "Utmost filial piety moves spirits; utmost harmony touches the unseen—the Odes say: 'When filial piety and brotherly duty reach their height, they reach spirits and gods and shine across the four seas.'

sentences.zh: '如此則孝順之道，無所不格。

translations.literal: Thus the way of filial obedience has nowhere it does not reach.
translations.idiomatic: So filial obedience leaves nowhere untouched.

sentences.zh: 願陛下念之，以濟黎庶。

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty will keep it in mind to succor the black-haired people.
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will keep it in mind to succor the people.

sentences.zh: 臣年志朽弊，識見昧然，在於愚慮，不敢不盡。

translations.literal: My years are decayed timber, my insight dim; in foolish counsel alone I dare not spare effort.
translations.idiomatic: My years are rotten timber, my sight dim; in foolish counsel I dare not spare effort.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「五更助三老以言至范，敷展德音。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The five elders assist the three elders in speaking the highest pattern and spreading virtuous words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The five elders aid the three elders in speaking the highest pattern and spreading virtue.

sentences.zh: 當克己復禮，以行來授。

translations.literal: I shall constrain myself and restore ritual, to carry what you impart."
translations.idiomatic: I shall restrain myself and restore ritual, to carry what you teach."

sentences.zh: 」禮畢，乃賜步挽一乘。

translations.literal: When the rites were finished, they were granted one palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites ended, each was granted a palanquin.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「夫尊老尚更，列聖同致，欽年敬德，綿哲齊軌。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Honoring elders and esteeming the five elders, the sacred kings shared this aim; revering years and honoring virtue, sages through the ages held one track.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Honoring elders and esteeming the five elders—the sacred kings shared this; revering years and honoring virtue—sages through the ages held one path.

sentences.zh: 朕雖道謝玄風，識昧睿則，然仰稟先誨，企遵猷旨。

translations.literal: Though my way falls short of the dark wind and my insight is dim to the bright pattern, yet I look up to receive earlier instructions and bend my steps to follow their intent.
translations.idiomatic: Though my way falls short of the dark wind and my sight is dim to the bright pattern, I look up to earlier teaching and bend my steps to follow it.

sentences.zh: 故推老以德，立更以元；

translations.literal: Therefore I exalt the aged through virtue and establish the five elders through primacy;
translations.idiomatic: So I exalt the aged through virtue and establish the five elders through primacy;

sentences.zh: 父焉斯彰，兄焉斯顯矣。

translations.literal: the father is thereby made manifest, the elder brother thereby displayed."
translations.idiomatic: the father shines forth, the elder brother stands clear."

sentences.zh: 前司徒西元、前鴻臚卿明根，並以沖德懸車，懿量歸老，故尊老以三，事更以五。

translations.literal: Former Minister of Works Wei Yuan and former Grand Herald Minggen—both suspended their lofty virtue in chariots and returned their fine measure in old age, so I honored the aged as three and served the five elders as five.
translations.idiomatic: Former Minister of Works Wei Yuan and former Grand Herald Minggen—both hung up their virtue and retired in honor, so I made three for the aged and five for the elders.

sentences.zh: 雖老、更非官，耄耋罔祿，然況事既高，宜加殊養。

translations.literal: Though the three elders and five elders are not offices, and the oldest receive no salary, yet when the matter stands so high, special nurture should be added.
translations.idiomatic: Though elders and five elders are not offices and the hoary receive no salary, the matter stands high and deserves special nurture.

sentences.zh: 三老可給上公祿，五更可食元卿俸。

translations.literal: The three elders may receive salary of the senior lord; the five elders may eat the stipend of the prime origin minister.
translations.idiomatic: The three elders may take a senior lord's stipend; the five elders a prime minister's pay.

sentences.zh: 供食之味，亦同其例。

translations.literal: The flavor of food offered shall match the same standard."
translations.idiomatic: The fare offered shall match the same standard."

sentences.zh: 」十七年，元疾篤，帝親省疾。

translations.literal: In year 17 Yuan fell gravely ill; the emperor visited him in person.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 Yuan fell gravely ill; the emperor visited him himself.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡景桓公，葬以殊禮，給羽葆鼓吹，假黃鉞，班劍四十人。

translations.literal: When he died he was given posthumous title Duke Huan of Jing; burial with special rites, feathered canopy and martial pipes granted, yellow battle-axe lent, forty guards of the sword.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was titled Duke Huan of Jing; burial with special rites, feathered canopy and martial pipes, yellow battle-axe on loan, forty sword guards.

sentences.zh: 子翊襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Yi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 遷洛，以山陽在畿內，改為博陵郡公。

translations.literal: When the capital moved to Luoyang, because Shanyang lay within the inner circuit, his title was changed to Duke of Boling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After the move to Luoyang, Shanyang lying within the inner circuit, his house was retitled Duke of Boling.

sentences.zh: 卒于恆州刺史，諡曰順。

translations.literal: He died as Governor of Heng Province; posthumous title: Compliant.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Governor of Heng; posthumous title: Compliant.

sentences.zh: 慕容白曜，慕容晃之玄孫也。

translations.literal: Murong Baiyao was the great-great-grandson of Murong Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Baiyao was the great-great-grandson of Murong Huang.

sentences.zh: 父琚，歷官以廉清著稱，賜爵高都侯。

translations.literal: His father Ju held office and was famed for integrity and purity; he was enfeoffed Marquis of Gaodu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ju was famed in office for integrity and was enfeoffed Marquis of Gaodu.

sentences.zh: 終尚書左丞，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: At death he was Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing; posthumous title: Simple.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing; posthumous title: Simple.

sentences.zh: 白曜少為中書吏，以敦直給事宮中。

translations.literal: Baiyao in youth was a clerk in the Secretariat; for honest uprightness he served in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Baiyao was a Secretariat clerk; honest and upright, he served in the palace.

sentences.zh: 襲爵，稍遷北部尚書。

translations.literal: He inherited the marquisate and was gradually promoted to Northern Minister of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the rank and rose to Northern Minister of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 文成崩，與乙渾共執朝政，遷尚書右僕射，進爵南鄉公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wencheng died, he and Yi Hun together held court power; he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and advanced to Duke of Nanxiang.
translations.idiomatic: At Wencheng's death he and Yi Hun seized court power; he became Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Duke of Nanxiang.

sentences.zh: 宋徐州刺史薛安都、兗州刺史畢眾敬並以城內附，詔鎮南大將軍尉元、鎮東將軍孔伯恭赴之。

translations.literal: Xue Andu, Governor of Xu Province in Song, and Bi Zhongjing, Governor of Yan, both surrendered their cities to the court; an edict ordered Grand General Who Guards the South Wei Yuan and Grand General Who Guards the East Kong Bogong to go.
translations.idiomatic: Song's Governors Xue Andu of Xu and Bi Zhongjing of Yan surrendered their cities; the court ordered Wei Yuan, Grand General Who Guards the South, and Kong Bogong, Grand General Who Guards the East, to go.

sentences.zh: 而宋東平太守申纂屯無鹽，并州刺史房崇吉屯鬥城，遏絕王使。

translations.literal: But Shen Zuan, Administrator of Dongping in Song, garrisoned Wuyan, and Fang Chongji, Inspector of Bing Province, held Doucheng, blocking and cutting off the king's envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Song's Dongping administrator Shen Zuan held Wuyan, and Bing Inspector Fang Chongji held Doucheng, blocking the king's envoys.

sentences.zh: 皇興初，加白曜使持節、都督軍事、征南大將軍，進爵上黨公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangxing, Baiyao was added bearer of the staff, commander of military affairs, and Grand General Who Campaigns South, and advanced to Duke of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: At Huangxing's opening Baiyao was made bearer of the staff, military commander, and Grand General Who Campaigns South, and advanced to Duke of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 屯碻磝，為諸軍後繼。

translations.literal: He encamped at Que'ao as rear for the armies.
translations.idiomatic: He encamped at Que'ao as army reserve.

sentences.zh: 白曜攻纂於無鹽，拔其東郭。

translations.literal: Baiyao attacked Shen Zuan at Wuyan and took the eastern wall.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao attacked Shen Zuan at Wuyan and stormed the eastern wall.

sentences.zh: 纂遁，遣兵追執之。

translations.literal: Zuan fled; Baiyao sent troops in pursuit and seized him.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan fled; troops pursued and seized him.

sentences.zh: 回攻鬥城。

translations.literal: He turned to attack Doucheng.
translations.idiomatic: He turned to attack Doucheng.

sentences.zh: 肥城戍主聞軍至，棄城遁走，獲粟三十萬石。

translations.literal: The garrison chief of Feicheng, hearing the army had come, abandoned the city and fled; they seized three hundred thousand shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Feicheng's garrison chief, hearing the army approach, fled; they took three hundred thousand shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 又下襲破麋溝、垣苗二戍，得粟十餘萬斛。

translations.literal: He next descended and stormed the garrisons of Migou and Yuanmiao, gaining more than a hundred thousand hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: He next stormed Migou and Yuanmiao, gaining more than a hundred thousand hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 由是軍糧充足。

translations.literal: Thus army provisions were ample.
translations.idiomatic: Army provisions were ample thereafter.

sentences.zh: 先是，淮陽公皮豹子再征垣苗不克，白曜一旬內頻拔四城，威震齊土。

translations.literal: Earlier Duke of Huaiyang Pi Baozi had twice attacked Yuanmiao without success; within ten days Baiyao took four cities in succession, and his prestige shook Qi lands.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Pi Baozi of Huaiyang had twice failed against Yuanmiao; Baiyao took four cities in ten days, and his name shook Qi.

sentences.zh: 獻文下詔褒美之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen issued an edict praising him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen issued an edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 鬥城不降，白曜縱兵陵城，殺數百人，崇吉夜遁。

translations.literal: Doucheng would not surrender; Baiyao let troops storm the walls and killed several hundred; Chongji fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Doucheng would not yield; Baiyao stormed the walls and killed hundreds; Chongji fled by night.

sentences.zh: 白曜撫其人，百姓懷之。

translations.literal: Baiyao comforted the people; the common folk were drawn to him.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao comforted the people; the folk clung to him.

sentences.zh: 獲崇吉母妻，待之以禮。

translations.literal: He captured Chongji's mother and wife and treated them with ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: He took Chongji's mother and wife and treated them with ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 宋遣將吳喜公欲冠彭城，鎮南大將軍尉元請濟師，獻文詔白曜赴之。

translations.literal: Song sent the general Wu Xi intending to relieve Pengcheng; Grand General Who Guards the South Wei Yuan requested reinforcements, and Emperor Xiaowen ordered Baiyao to go.
translations.idiomatic: Song sent Wu Xi to relieve Pengcheng; Wei Yuan asked for reinforcements, and Xiaowen ordered Baiyao there.

sentences.zh: 白曜到瑕丘，遇患，因停。

translations.literal: Baiyao reached Xianqiu but fell ill and halted.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao reached Xianqiu, fell ill, and halted.

sentences.zh: 會崇吉與從弟法壽盜宋盤陽城以贖母妻。

translations.literal: It happened that Chongji and his younger cousin Fashou seized Song's Panyang city to ransom mother and wife.
translations.idiomatic: Chongji and his cousin Fashou then seized Song's Panyang to ransom mother and wife.

sentences.zh: 白曜遣將軍長孫觀等率騎入自馬耳關赴之。

translations.literal: Baiyao sent General Zhangsun Guan and others with cavalry in through Ma'er Pass to go to their aid.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao sent Zhangsun Guan and cavalry through Ma'er Pass to their aid.

sentences.zh: 觀至盤陽，諸縣悉降。

translations.literal: When Guan reached Panyang, all counties submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Guan reached Panyang; every county submitted.

sentences.zh: 白曜自瑕丘進攻曆城。

translations.literal: Baiyao advanced from Xianqiu to attack Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao advanced from Xianqiu against Licheng.

sentences.zh: 二年，崔道固及兗州刺史梁鄒守將劉休賓並面縛而降。

translations.literal: In year 2 Cui Daogu and Liu Xiubin, garrison chief of Liangzou in Yan Province, both came bound to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 Cui Daogu and Yan's Liangzou garrison chief Liu Xiubin came bound to surrender.

sentences.zh: 白曜皆釋之。

translations.literal: Baiyao released them all.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao released them all.

sentences.zh: 送道固、休賓及其僚屬于京師。

translations.literal: He sent Daogu, Xiubin, and their staffs to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Daogu, Xiubin, and their staffs to the capital.

sentences.zh: 後乃徙二城人望於下館，朝廷置平齊郡懷甯、歸安二縣以居之。

translations.literal: Only afterward were the leading families of the two cities moved to Xiaguan; the court established Pingqi Commandery with counties Huaining and Gui'an to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: Later the leading families of both cities were moved to Xiaguan; the court set Pingqi Commandery with Huaining and Gui'an to house them.

sentences.zh: 自余悉為奴婢，分賜百官。

translations.literal: The rest were all made slaves and distributed among the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: The rest were enslaved and given to officials.

sentences.zh: 白曜雖在軍旅，而接待人物，寬和有禮。

translations.literal: Though Baiyao was on campaign, he received men with courtesy, broad and kindly.
translations.idiomatic: Though at war, Baiyao received men with broad courtesy.

sentences.zh: 所獲崇吉母妻、申纂婦女，皆別營安置，不令士卒喧雜。

translations.literal: Chongji's mother and wife and Shen Zuan's women were all quartered separately; he did not let soldiers make uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Chongji's mother and wife and Shen Zuan's women were quartered apart; he kept soldiers from disorder.

sentences.zh: 及進克東陽，擒沈文秀。

translations.literal: When he next took Dongyang, he captured Shen Wenxiu.
translations.idiomatic: When he took Dongyang he captured Shen Wenxiu.

sentences.zh: 凡獲倉粟八十五萬斛。

translations.literal: In all they seized eight hundred fifty thousand hu of granary grain.
translations.idiomatic: In all they took eight hundred fifty thousand hu from granaries.

sentences.zh: 始末三年，築圍攻擊，雖士卒死傷，無多怨叛。

translations.literal: From first to last three years, building siegeworks and attacking—though soldiers died and were wounded, there was little mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Three years of siege and assault cost many lives, yet little mutiny.

sentences.zh: 三齊欣然，安堵樂業。

translations.literal: The three Qi districts were glad; people settled and worked in peace.
translations.idiomatic: The three Qi districts were glad; people settled in peace.

sentences.zh: 克城之日，以沈文秀抗倨不為之拜，忿而撾撻，唯以此見譏。

translations.literal: On the day the city fell, because Shen Wenxiu stood proud and would not bow, Baiyao in anger had him beaten—only this drew censure.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell Shen Wenxiu would not bow; Baiyao in anger had him beaten—only this drew blame.

sentences.zh: 以功拜開府儀同三司、都督、青州刺史，進爵濟南王。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed Opening the Government with ceremonial rank equal to the Three Excellencies, Commander-in-Chief, Governor of Qing Province, and advanced to Prince of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was made Opening the Government with Three Excellencies' ceremonial rank, Commander-in-Chief, Governor of Qing, and Prince of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 初，乙渾專權，白曜頗所挾附，後緣此以為責。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yi Hun monopolized power, Baiyao had leaned on him somewhat; later he was blamed for this.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi Hun held sole power Baiyao had leaned on him; later that became his charge.

sentences.zh: 四年，見誅，雲謀反叛，時論冤之。

translations.literal: In year 4 he was executed on the charge of plotting rebellion; opinion at the time called it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he was executed for alleged rebellion; opinion called it unjust.

sentences.zh: 白曜少子真安，年十一，聞父被執，將自殺。

translations.literal: Baiyao's youngest son Zhen'an, eleven years old, hearing his father was seized, was about to kill himself.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Zhen'an, eleven, hearing his father seized, meant to kill himself.

sentences.zh: 家人止之曰：「輕重未可知。

translations.literal: The household stopped him, saying: "The gravity is not yet known."
translations.idiomatic: Kin stopped him: "The charge is not yet known."

sentences.zh: 」真安曰：「王位高功重，若小罪，終不至此。

translations.literal: Zhen'an said: "A princely rank and weighty merit—if a small fault, it would never come to this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen'an said: "Prince's rank and great merit—if a small fault, it would never come to this.

sentences.zh: 我不忍見父之死。

translations.literal: I cannot bear to see my father's death."
translations.idiomatic: I cannot bear to see my father die."

sentences.zh: 」遂自縊。

translations.literal: He thereupon hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: He hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 太和中，著作佐郎成淹上表理白曜，孝文覽表嘉湣之。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era Palace Gentleman Author Cheng Yan memorialized in Baiyao's defense; Emperor Xiaowen read it and was moved to pity.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe Author Cheng Yan memorialized for Baiyao; Xiaowen read it and was moved to pity.

sentences.zh: 白曜弟子契，輕薄無檢。

translations.literal: Baiyao's nephew Qi was frivolous and without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew Qi was frivolous and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 太和初，以名家子擢為中散，遷宰官中散。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe, as a son of a great house he was promoted to Palace Cadet and transferred to Palace Cadet of the Palace Steward.
translations.idiomatic: At Taihe's opening, as a great-house son he became Palace Cadet, then Palace Cadet of the Palace Steward.

sentences.zh: 南安王楨有貪暴之響，遣中散閭文祖詣長安察之。

translations.literal: Prince of Nan'an Zhen had a reputation for greed and violence; he sent Palace Cadet Lu Wenzu to Chang'an to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Nan'an Zhen was known for greed and cruelty; he sent Lu Wenzu to Chang'an to investigate.

sentences.zh: 文祖受楨金寶之賂，為楨隱而不言。

translations.literal: Wenzu accepted gold and treasure from Zhen and concealed it without speaking.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzu took Zhen's gold and treasure and concealed the truth.

sentences.zh: 事發，太后引見群臣，謂曰：「前論貪清，皆云克修。

translations.literal: When the matter broke, the empress dowager received the ministers and said: "Earlier when we discussed greed and purity, all said they could discipline themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When it broke, the empress dowager received the ministers and said: "When we discussed greed and purity, all claimed discipline.

sentences.zh: 文祖時亦在中，後竟犯法。

translations.literal: Wenzu was then among them, yet afterward he violated the law.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzu was among them—yet he broke the law.

sentences.zh: 以此言之，人心信不可知。

translations.literal: From this one may say the human heart truly cannot be known."
translations.idiomatic: So the human heart cannot be known."

sentences.zh: 」孝文曰：「卿等自審不勝貪心者，聽辭位歸第。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen said: "If you yourselves judge you cannot overcome greedy hearts, you may resign office and return home."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen said: "Who judges himself unable to master greed may resign and go home."

sentences.zh: 」契進曰：「小人之心無定，而帝王之法有常。

translations.literal: Qi stepped forward and said: "The small man's heart has no fixity, while the emperor's law has constancy.
translations.idiomatic: Qi stepped forward: "The small man's heart has no fixity; the emperor's law is constant.

sentences.zh: 以無恆之心奉有常之法，非所克堪。

translations.literal: To serve constant law with an inconstant heart is not what one can bear.
translations.idiomatic: To serve constant law with an inconstant heart is beyond me.

sentences.zh: 乞垂退免。

translations.literal: I beg to be dismissed and relieved."
translations.idiomatic: I beg dismissal."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「契若知心不可常，即知貪之惡矣，何為求退？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If Qi knows the heart cannot be constant, he knows the evil of greed—why seek dismissal?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "If Qi knows the heart cannot be constant, he knows greed's evil—why resign?

sentences.zh: 」遷宰官令，賜爵定陶男。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Palace Steward and enfeoffed Baron of Dingtao.
translations.idiomatic: He became Director of the Palace Steward and Baron of Dingtao.

sentences.zh: 後卒于都督、朔州刺史，諡曰克。

translations.literal: Later he died as Commander-in-Chief and Governor of Shuo Province; posthumous title: Victorious.
translations.idiomatic: He later died as Commander-in-Chief and Governor of Shuo; posthumous title: Victorious.

sentences.zh: 初，慕容氏破後，種族仍繁。

translations.literal: Earlier, after the Murong house was broken, the clan remained numerous.
translations.idiomatic: After the Murong house fell, the clan remained numerous.

sentences.zh: 天賜末，頗忌而誅之。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tianshi era they were much feared and executed.
translations.idiomatic: At Tianshi's end they were feared and many were killed.

sentences.zh: 時有免者，不敢復姓，皆以輿為氏。

translations.literal: Those who escaped did not dare resume the surname; all took Yu as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: Survivors dared not resume the surname; all took Yu as clan name.

sentences.zh: 延昌末，詔復舊姓。

translations.literal: At the end of Yanchang an edict restored the old surname.
translations.idiomatic: At Yanchang's end an edict restored the old surname.

sentences.zh: 而其子女先入掖庭者，猶號慕容，特多於他族。

translations.literal: Yet sons and daughters who had earlier entered the rear palace still bore the name Murong—far more than other clans.
translations.idiomatic: Sons and daughters already in the rear palace still bore Murong—more than any other clan.

sentences.zh: 宇文福，其先南單于之遠屬也。

translations.literal: Yu Wenfu was of the remote line of the Southern Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wenfu descended from the Southern Chanyu's distant line.

sentences.zh: 世為擁部大人。

translations.literal: For generations his house were chiefs of the Yong tribe.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his house were chiefs of the Yong department.

sentences.zh: 祖活撥，仕慕容垂為唐郡內史、遼東公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Huobo served Murong Chui as Inner Secretary of Tang Commandery and Duke of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Huobo served Murong Chui as Tang Commandery's inner secretary and Duke of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 道武之平慕容氏，活撥入魏，為第一客。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daowu pacified the Murong house, Huobo entered Wei as the foremost guest.
translations.idiomatic: When Daowu pacified the Murong house, Huobo entered Wei as foremost guest.

sentences.zh: 福少驍果，有膂力。

translations.literal: Fu in youth was valiant and had strength of body.
translations.idiomatic: Fu in youth was valiant and powerfully built.

sentences.zh: 太和中，累遷都牧給事。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he was repeatedly promoted to Master of Pasturage attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe he rose to Master of Pasturage attendant.

sentences.zh: 及遷洛，敕福檢牧馬所。

translations.literal: When the capital moved to Luoyang, an order charged Fu to inspect the horse pastures.
translations.idiomatic: At the move to Luoyang he was ordered to inspect the horse pastures.

sentences.zh: 福規石濟以西，河內以東，拒黃河南北千里為牧地，今之馬場是也。

translations.literal: Fu marked west of Shiji to east of Henei, a thousand li north and south of the Yellow River, as pasture—the present horse grounds.
translations.idiomatic: He marked west of Shiji to east of Henei, a thousand li along the Yellow River north and south—the present horse grounds.

sentences.zh: 及徙代移雜畜牧於其所，福善於將養，並無損耗。

translations.literal: When mixed herds were moved from Dai to that place, Fu was skilled in tending them and none were lost.
translations.idiomatic: When mixed herds were moved from Dai there, Fu tended them without loss.

sentences.zh: 孝文嘉之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen praised him.

sentences.zh: 尋補司衛監。

translations.literal: Shortly he was made Supervisor of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Supervisor of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 後以勳封襄樂縣男，歷位太僕卿、都官尚書、營州大中正、瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: Later for merit he was enfeoffed Baron of Xiangle and held the posts of Grand Herald, Director of the Department of State Affairs, Grand Umpire of Ying Province, and Governor of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later for merit he was Baron of Xiangle, then Grand Herald, Director of the Department of State Affairs, Grand Umpire of Ying, and Governor of Ying.

sentences.zh: 性忠清，在公嚴毅，以信御人，甚得聲譽。

translations.literal: By nature loyal and pure, stern in public office, he ruled men by trust and won great repute.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal and pure by nature, stern in office, he ruled by trust and won great repute.

sentences.zh: 後除都督懷朔、沃野、武川三鎮諸軍事、懷朔鎮將。

translations.literal: Later he was made Commander-in-Chief of military affairs at the three garrisons of Huaishuo, Woye, and Wuchuan and Garrison Commander of Huaishuo.
translations.idiomatic: Later he commanded the three garrisons of Huaishuo, Woye, and Wuchuan and was Garrison Commander of Huaishuo.

sentences.zh: 至鎮卒，諡曰貞惠。

translations.literal: He died at his post; posthumous title: Loyal and Kind.
translations.idiomatic: He died at his post; posthumous title: Loyal and Kind.

sentences.zh: 子延，字慶壽，體貌魁岸，眉目疏朗。

translations.literal: His son Yan, styled Qinghou, had a towering frame and open, sparse brows.
translations.idiomatic: Son Yan, styled Qinghou, was tall and broad, with open, sparse brows.

sentences.zh: 位員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: He held the post of Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant.

sentences.zh: 以父老，詔聽隨侍在瀛州。

translations.literal: Because his father was old, an edict permitted him to attend and wait in Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father being old, an edict let him wait on him in Ying.

sentences.zh: 屬大乘妖黨突入州城，延率奴客逆戰，身被重瘡。

translations.literal: When the Mahayana cultists burst into the prefectural city, Yan led household slaves and guests to meet them in battle and was heavily wounded.
translations.idiomatic: When Mahayana fanatics burst into the city, Yan led slaves and guests to fight and was heavily wounded.

sentences.zh: 賊縱火燒齋閣，福時在內。

translations.literal: The bandits set fire to the study hall; Fu was then within.
translations.idiomatic: They set fire to the study; Fu was inside.

sentences.zh: 延突火入，抱福出外，支體灼爛，鬢髮盡焦。

translations.literal: Yan rushed through the flames, carried Fu out; his limbs were burned raw, hair and temples scorched away.
translations.idiomatic: Yan rushed through flame, carried Fu out; limbs burned raw, hair and temples scorched away.

sentences.zh: 於是勒眾與賊苦戰，賊乃散走，以此見稱。

translations.literal: Thereupon he rallied the host to fight the bandits bitterly; the bandits scattered—for this he won praise.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied men and fought bitterly; the bandits scattered—he won praise for this.

sentences.zh: 累遷直寢。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Direct Attendant of the Inner Quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Direct Attendant of the Inner Quarters.

sentences.zh: 與万俟晗鬼奴戰，沒。

translations.literal: Fighting Wanqi Han the Ghost Slave, he was killed in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting Wanqi Han the Ghost Slave, he fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 論曰：古弼軍謀經國，有柱石之量；

translations.literal: Discussion: Gu Bi's military plans sustained the state and had the measure of a pillar;
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Gu Bi's stratagems sustained the state—he had a pillar's measure;

sentences.zh: 張黎誠謹廉方，以勳舊見重。

translations.literal: Zhang Li was sincere, careful, pure, and square, honored as an old merit-holder.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Li was sincere, careful, pure, and square, honored among old merit-holders.

sentences.zh: 並纖介之間，一朝隕覆。

translations.literal: Both in a fiber's breadth fell in a single morning.
translations.idiomatic: Both fell in a fiber's breadth in a single morning.

sentences.zh: 宥及十世，乃徒言耳。

translations.literal: Pardon reaching ten generations—only empty words.
translations.idiomatic: Pardon to ten generations—only empty words.

sentences.zh: 劉潔咎之徒也；

translations.literal: Liu Jie was a man of blame;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jie was a man of blame;

sentences.zh: 丘堆敗以亡身。

translations.literal: Qiu Dui failed and lost his life.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Dui failed and lost his life.

sentences.zh: 娥清、伊珝俱以材力見用，而珝以謀猷取異，其殆優乎。

translations.literal: E Qing and Yi Xu were both employed for strength and talent, while Xu won distinction through stratagem—is he perhaps the better?
translations.idiomatic: E Qing and Yi Xu were used for strength; Xu won distinction by stratagem—perhaps the better?

sentences.zh: 乙瑰之驍猛，周幾之智勇，代田之騎射，其位遇豈徒然也。

translations.literal: Yi Gui's fierceness, Zhou Ji's wisdom and courage, Dou Daitian's horsemanship and archery—their appointments were hardly accidental.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Gui's fierceness, Zhou Ji's wit and courage, Dou Daitian's riding and bow—hardly accidental posts.

sentences.zh: 車伊洛宅心自遠，豈常戎乎。

translations.literal: Che Yiluo's heart dwelt far from common tribesmen—was he merely a routine warrior?
translations.idiomatic: Che Yiluo's heart stood far from common tribesmen—hardly a routine warrior.

sentences.zh: 王洛兒、車路頭、盧魯元、陳建、來大幹、宿石，或誠發於衷，竭節危難；

translations.literal: Wang Luo'er, Che Lutou, Lu Luyuan, Chen Jian, Lai Dagan, and Su Shi—some with sincerity from the breast, exhausting loyalty in peril;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Luo'er, Che Lutou, Lu Luyuan, Chen Jian, Lai Dagan, Su Shi—some sincere to the bone, loyal in peril;

sentences.zh: 或忠存衛主，義足感人。

translations.literal: some guarding the ruler in loyalty, righteousness enough to move men.
translations.idiomatic: some guarding the ruler, righteousness enough to move men.

sentences.zh: 苟非志烈，亦何能若此。

translations.literal: Had they not been men of fierce will, how could they have done so?
translations.idiomatic: Without fierce will, how could they?

sentences.zh: 宜其生受恩遇，歿盡哀榮。

translations.literal: Small wonder they received favor in life and full mourning glory in death.
translations.idiomatic: No wonder they were favored in life and mourned in full glory at death.

sentences.zh: 至如安國，以至覆亡，害盈之義也。

translations.literal: As for Anguo, he reached ruin—also the meaning of harm overflowing.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo reached ruin—the meaning of harm overflowing.

sentences.zh: 周觀、尉撥、陸真、呂洛拔等，咸以勇毅自進，而觀竟致貶黜，異夫數子者矣。

translations.literal: Zhou Guan, Wei Bo, Lu Zhen, Lu Luoba, and the rest all advanced through courage and resolution, yet Guan in the end met demotion—different from those several.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Guan, Wei Bo, Lu Zhen, Lu Luoba advanced by courage; yet Guan was demoted—unlike the rest.

sentences.zh: 薛彪子世載強正，曇珍克盛家聲，美矣乎！

translations.literal: Xue Biaozi carried stern rectitude through generations; Yan Zhen sustained the family name—beautiful, was it not!
translations.idiomatic: Xue Biaozi bore stern rectitude through generations; Yan Zhen sustained the house—beautiful!

sentences.zh: 魏之諸將，罕方面之績。

translations.literal: Among Wei's generals, regional achievements were rare.
translations.idiomatic: Among Wei's generals, few won regional achievement.

sentences.zh: 尉元以寬雅之風，膺將帥之任，威名遠被，位極公老，自致乞言之地，無乃近代之一人歟！

translations.literal: Wei Yuan with his broad, elegant manner undertook command, his prestige reaching far, rank topping the elder statesmen, reaching on his own the place of one who begs to speak—was he not perhaps the one man of recent times!
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuan's broad, elegant manner bore command; prestige reached far, rank topped the elders, and he won on his own the place of one who begs to speak—perhaps the one man of recent times!

sentences.zh: 白曜出專薄伐，席捲三齊，考績圖勞，固不細矣。

translations.literal: Baiyao went forth on thin campaigns, swept the three Qi, and in reckoning merit on the map his service was no small thing.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao went forth on lean campaigns, swept the three Qi—in merit reckoned on the map his service was no small thing.

sentences.zh: 而功名難處，追猜嬰戮。

translations.literal: Yet merit and fame are hard to hold; pursued by suspicion he met the blade.
translations.idiomatic: Yet merit and fame are hard to hold; suspicion pursued him to the blade.

sentences.zh: 宥賢議勤，未聞於斯日也。

translations.literal: Pardoning the worthy and weighing merit—on that day it was not heard.
translations.idiomatic: Pardoning worth and weighing merit—that day it was not heard.

sentences.zh: 和其奴之貞正，苟頹之剛直，宇文福之氣幹，咸亦有用之士乎！

translations.literal: He Qinu's uprightness, Gou Tui's stern rectitude, Yu Wenfu's force of spirit—they too were men of use, were they not!
translations.idiomatic: He Qinu's uprightness, Gou Tui's stern rectitude, Yu Wenfu's force of spirit—they too were useful men!
